A is partly right because he did collect authentic songs, but the text says fitting tunes into conventional harmonies was what earlier composers did, and Bartók went beyond direct quotation. B mentions the urban melodies from the text, but his recordings actually showed him the limits of those melodies and harmonies. D builds on the fact that he collected thousands of songs, but the text never compares him to other collectors or calls his compositions a record of folk traditions.
input.design: To answer, you have to connect two pieces of information: what the recordings revealed and how Bartók went beyond quoting songs. A and D each start from a true detail but twist it, so you must compare them closely to rule them out.

input.passage: Conventional lithium-ion batteries rely on organic liquid electrolytes that begin to break down when the voltage across them climbs too high, which limits how much energy a cell can store. Ionic liquids—salts that remain liquid at room temperature—have drawn attention because many of them resist decomposition across a much wider voltage range. Researchers caution, however, that this advantage is not unconditional: even trace amounts of water absorbed from the air can ______ an ionic liquid's stability, narrowing its usable voltage window so much that it performs little better than the conventional electrolytes it was meant to replace.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: disguise
regulate
undermine
reveal
input.explanation: 지문은 미량의 수분이 이온성 액체의 전압 창을 좁혀 기존 전해질보다 나을 게 없게 만든다고 말하므로, 빈칸에는 안정성을 '약화시키다'라는 뜻이 필요하고 C(undermine)가 이에 맞습니다. A(disguise)는 안정성을 숨긴다는 뜻이라 실제로 성능이 떨어진다는 내용과 맞지 않습니다. B(regulate)는 수분이 안정성에 영향을 준다는 점은 담지만, 조절한다는 중립적인 의미일 뿐 안정성이 떨어진다는 방향은 담지 못합니다. D(reveal)는 수분이 숨어 있던 한계를 드러낸다고 읽을 수도 있지만, 지문은 수분이 안정성을 직접 떨어뜨린다고 말하므로 맞지 않습니다.
input.explanation_en: The text says trace water narrows the ionic liquid's voltage window until it performs little better than conventional electrolytes, so the blank needs a word meaning "weaken." That makes C (undermine) the answer. A (disguise) means to hide the stability, but the text describes performance actually getting worse. B (regulate) captures that water affects stability, but it's a neutral word meaning "control," so it misses the direction of harm. D (reveal) could suggest water exposes a hidden limit, but the text says water directly reduces stability rather than uncovering it.
input.design: 'unconditional' 단서와 '전압 창이 좁아진다'는 결과를 연결해야 하는 두 단계 판단 문항입니다. B와 D는 '영향을 준다'거나 '한계를 드러낸다'는 그럴듯한 해석이 가능해서 정답과 비교해 봐야 배제됩니다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Anthropologist Josephine Powell studied carpet weaving in rural Anatolia (present-day Türkiye) from the 1970s to the 1990s.
- In many Anatolian villages, carpets were woven at home as a cottage industry.
- Women and girls did most of the knotting and weaving on household looms.
- Men usually sheared the sheep and took finished carpets to sell at town markets.
- Powell collected more than 1,000 textiles and weaving tools during her research.
input.question: The student wants to describe how tasks were split between men and women in Anatolian carpet production. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In rural Anatolia, anthropologist Josephine Powell studied carpet weaving from the 1970s to the 1990s.
In rural Anatolia, carpets were often woven at home, making weaving a cottage industry in many villages.
In rural Anatolia, Josephine Powell collected more than 1,000 textiles and weaving tools during her research.
In rural Anatolia, women and girls did most of the knotting and weaving, while men sheared the sheep and sold the finished carpets.
input.design: 목표가 성별 분업에 관한 두 메모와 직접 대응하는 쉬운 문항이며, 오답은 같은 문장 틀에 목표와 무관한 메모(연구자, 가내공업, 수집품)를 넣었다.
input.explanation: 목표는 카펫 생산에서 남녀가 일을 어떻게 나누었는지 설명하는 것이다. D는 여성은 매듭짓기와 직조를 맡고, 남성은 양털 깎기와 판매를 맡았다고 밝혀 남녀 양쪽의 역할을 모두 보여 준다. A는 연구 기간만 말할 뿐 분업은 언급하지 않는다. B는 직조가 가내공업이었다는 사실만 제시하고 누가 어떤 일을 했는지는 말하지 않는다. C는 Powell의 수집품에 관한 내용이라 목표와 관계가 없다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to describe how men and women split the work of making carpets. D does this because it says women and girls did the knotting and weaving, while men sheared the sheep and sold the carpets, so it covers both sides of the division. A only gives the years of Powell's research and says nothing about who did which tasks. B only says weaving was a cottage industry, without saying who did what. C is about Powell's collection, which has nothing to do with the goal.

input.passage: When the power failed, Danny lit a stub of candle and set the old checkerboard on the kitchen table. His grandson, Eli, wanted to know how miners had found their way underground before electric lamps, and Danny answered between jumps of his red kings. The questions that the boy asked between moves, whispered as though the dark itself might be listening, ______ gradually from the candle's flicker to whether the mine would still be open by the time he grew up.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: drifts
drifted
was drifting
drifting
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'The questions'이고, 'that the boy asked between moves'와 'whispered as though...listening'은 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 그래서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 맞는 정동사가 와야 하고, 지문 전체가 과거 시제(failed, lit, wanted)이므로 과거형 B 'drifted'가 정답이다. A 'drifts'는 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'dark'에 맞춘 단수 현재형이라 수도 시제도 맞지 않는다. C 'was drifting'은 과거 시제는 맞지만 단수 동사라서 복수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. D 'drifting'은 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The questions." The phrases "that the boy asked between moves" and "whispered as though the dark itself might be listening" only modify that subject. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, and since the passage is told in the past tense (failed, lit, wanted), B, "drifted," is correct. A, "drifts," agrees with the nearby singular noun "dark" instead of the real subject, and it's also in the wrong tense. C, "was drifting," gets the past tense right, but it's singular, so it doesn't agree with the plural subject. D, "drifting," is a participle, which would leave the sentence with no main verb.
input.design: A long relative clause and participial phrase come between the plural subject and the blank, and the singular noun "dark" sits right before the blank. To get the answer, students have to check agreement and then confirm the tense, which rules out C, the partially correct option.

content.text:
Easy 난이도로 하나의 규칙을 묻는다. 시제 일관성: 과거 시제 서사에서 동사를 과거형으로 맞추는 문제다.

Passage: "Every spring, Hans returned to his small allotment garden on the edge of Berlin. Kneeling in the dark soil, he ______ the tomato seedlings in three crooked rows, exactly as he had promised Anna thirty years earlier, the week before she boarded the train to Prague."

Options: A) sets B) will set C) has set D) set — "set"는 과거형이다. 다만 "set"는 현재형일 수도 있고, 주어가 he이므로 현재형이면 "sets"가 된다. 따라서 "set"는 과거형이 맞다. 동사를 plant로 바꿔 보면 오답이 plants / will plant / has planted, 정답이 planted가 된다. 이렇게 하는 편이 더 명확하다.

input.passage: Every spring, Hans returned to his small allotment garden on the edge of Berlin. Kneeling in the dark soil, he ______ the tomato seedlings in three crooked rows, exactly as he had promised Anna thirty years earlier, the week before she boarded the train to Prague.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: plants
will plant
has planted
planted
input.explanation: 이 지문은 returned, had promised, boarded 등 과거 시제로 서술되므로 빈칸의 동사도 과거 시제여야 한다. 따라서 과거형인 D가 정답이다. A는 현재 시제라 과거 서사와 어긋난다. B는 미래 시제로 매년 봄 이미 일어난 행동을 나타낼 수 없다. C는 현재완료로 과거 서사의 시간 틀과 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The passage tells the story in the past tense with verbs such as "returned," "had promised," and "boarded," so the verb in the blank should also be in the past tense. That makes D, the past-tense form, correct. A uses the present tense, which clashes with the past-tense narration. B uses the future tense, but the sentence describes something Hans already did each spring. C uses the present perfect, which doesn't fit the past-tense time frame of the story.
input.design: 수식어가 있지만 단서가 분명한 시제 일관성 한 가지 규칙만 묻는 easy 문항이다. 오답은 현재형, 미래형, 현재완료형이다.

input.passage: Graphene aerogels, made by freeze-drying a suspension of graphene oxide sheets and then chemically reducing the resulting scaffold, are among the lightest solids ever produced, with some samples weighing less than the air they displace. Because more than 99 percent of their volume is empty space, many engineers assumed they would be excellent thermal insulators, since heat travels poorly through gas-filled pores. __Yet early measurements by materials scientist Hu Liang's team showed that their aerogels conducted heat noticeably better than expected for their density.__ The team traced the problem to the graphene sheets themselves: graphene carries heat extremely well along its plane, so wherever sheets touched and formed continuous walls, heat flowed quickly through the solid network. By adjusting the freezing rate to produce thinner, more fragmented walls with fewer sheet-to-sheet contacts, the researchers lowered the material's conductivity to levels rivaling the best commercial insulators.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a measurement that confirms the engineers' reasoning about how heat moves through gas-filled pores.
It presents a finding that runs counter to an expectation and sets up the explanation and remedy that follow.
It presents a finding that shows graphene aerogels are unsuitable for insulation, a conclusion the rest of the text supports.
It presents a finding that explains why freeze-drying produces some of the lightest solids ever made.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 기공이 많으니 단열이 뛰어날 것이라는 기대와 달리 열전도가 예상보다 높았다는 결과를 제시하고, 이어지는 문장들이 그 원인(그래핀 시트 접촉)과 해결책(동결 속도 조절)을 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 측정이 기대를 확인한 것이 아니라 뒤집었으므로 틀리다. C는 문제 제기라는 점은 맞지만, 글 후반에서 상용 단열재 수준으로 개선했으므로 '부적합하다'는 결론을 뒷받침하지 않는다. D는 가벼움을 다룬 첫 문장과 관련 있을 뿐, 밑줄 문장은 열전도에 관한 것이다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet." It reports that the aerogels conducted heat better than expected, which goes against the assumption that all those gas-filled pores would make them excellent insulators. The rest of the text then explains the cause (graphene sheets touching each other) and the fix (changing the freezing rate), so B is correct. A is wrong because the measurement contradicts the engineers' reasoning instead of confirming it. C correctly sees that the sentence raises a problem, but the text ends with the conductivity brought down to the level of top commercial insulators, so it never concludes that the aerogels are unsuitable. D links the sentence to the first sentence about lightness, but the underlined sentence is about heat conduction, not about why the material is so light.
input.design: To answer, students must connect the "Yet" contrast with both what comes before and what comes after. C and A are tempting because they half-fit: C matches the "problem" reading, and A is tied to the engineers' reasoning.

input.passage: In Portugal, which supplies roughly half of the world's cork, the bark of the cork oak can be stripped only once every nine years, and a tree yields its first commercially usable bark only after it is about forty years old. Because a newly planted grove will not repay its owner for decades, many landowners in the Alentejo region manage their montados as multigenerational holdings, with planting decisions made by one generation and the main harvests collected by its grandchildren. Economists studying the sector argue that this long horizon, rather than low labor costs or favorable climate alone, explains why Portuguese producers have kept their dominant share of international supply: competitors elsewhere have found it hard to justify investments whose returns arrive so slowly, while Portuguese families inherit groves that are already productive.
input.question: According to the text, what do economists consider the main reason Portugal has stayed the leading source of cork in world markets?
options: Portuguese producers pay lower wages to harvesters than rival producers do, which keeps the price of their cork below that of competitors.
Portuguese producers benefit from a climate that lets cork oaks regrow their bark faster than trees elsewhere, allowing more frequent harvests.
Portuguese producers hold groves passed down through families over generations, sparing them slow-paying investments that discourage rivals.
Portuguese producers harvest the bark of young trees earlier than rivals do, which lets new groves start earning a return within a few years.
input.explanation: 경제학자들은 낮은 인건비나 기후만이 아니라 긴 투자 시간 지평, 즉 이미 생산성이 있는 숲을 상속받는 구조 때문에 경쟁자들이 따라오지 못한다고 보므로 C가 정답이다. A는 지문에 나오는 인건비를 언급하지만, 지문은 그것이 주된 이유가 아니라고 말한다. B는 기후를 언급하지만 이 역시 부정된 요인이고, 수확 주기는 9년으로 고정되어 있다. D는 첫 수확까지 약 40년이 걸린다는 내용과 정반대이다.
input.explanation_en: C is correct. The economists say the key factor is the long time horizon: Portuguese families inherit groves that are already productive, while rivals elsewhere hesitate to make investments that take decades to pay off. A mentions labor costs, which do appear in the text, but the passage says this factor does not explain Portugal's lead. B mentions climate, which is set aside in the same way, and the text says the harvest cycle is fixed at nine years. D contradicts the text, since trees produce usable bark only at about forty years old.
input.design: 문항을 풀려면 '~ rather than ... alone' 대조 구문을 해석하고, 그 결과를 상속받은 숲과 경쟁자들의 투자 기피라는 두 정보와 연결해야 한다. 오답 A와 B는 지문에 나오는 요인을 재활용한 미끼이며, 네 선택지는 모두 같은 문장 틀로 썼다.

input.passage:
Text 1
Linguistic anthropologist Elinor Ochs argued that most linguistic features do not point to social categories such as gender directly. Instead, a particle or intonation pattern first signals a stance, such as hesitancy or forcefulness, and listeners then link that stance to a social identity. On this view, a sentence-final particle used often by women in Japanese marks gentleness, and only through that stance comes to be associated with femininity.

Text 2
Some sociolinguists studying workplace talk report that certain hedges, like "sort of," are so routinely tied to junior employees that listeners infer rank the instant they hear them, with no apparent attention to stance. Yet these researchers also find that the same hedges, when used by senior managers, are heard as diplomatic rather than subordinate. That reversal suggests listeners still read the hedge first as a stance, tentativeness, whose social meaning depends on who is speaking.
input.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Ochs' claim in Text 1 about how linguistic features come to be associated with social identities?
options: By suggesting that evidence seeming to challenge the claim, once examined more closely, actually supports it
By suggesting that evidence from workplace talk shows the claim applies to Japanese but not to English
By suggesting that evidence of listeners inferring rank instantly shows the claim to be mistaken
By suggesting that evidence about senior managers shows the claim exaggerates the importance of who is speaking
input.explanation: Text 1의 Ochs는 언어 형태가 먼저 태도(stance)를 나타내고, 그 태도를 거쳐 사회적 정체성과 연결된다고 주장한다. Text 2는 처음에 'sort of'가 태도 없이 곧바로 직급을 나타내는 것처럼 보인다는 반례를 소개하지만, 고위 관리자가 쓰면 의미가 뒤바뀐다는 점을 들어 결국 청자가 먼저 태도를 읽는다고 결론 내리므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 언어 간 차이를 주장하지 않으므로 틀리다. C는 Text 2 앞부분만 훑어 읽으면 고를 수 있지만, Text 2는 그 증거를 뒤집는다. D는 Text 2가 오히려 화자가 누구인지가 사회적 의미를 결정한다고 말하므로 틀리다.
input.explanation_en: In Text 1, Ochs claims that a linguistic feature first signals a stance, and only through that stance does it become linked to a social identity. Text 2 starts with what looks like a counterexample: "sort of" seems to signal rank right away. Then it shows that the same hedge means something different when senior managers use it, and it concludes that listeners still read stance first, so A is correct. B is wrong because Text 2 never says the claim works for one language and not another. C is tempting if you only skim the first part of Text 2, but the author goes on to reject that interpretation. D is wrong because Text 2 says the speaker's identity is what shapes the social meaning, which is the opposite of saying Ochs overstates it.
input.design: 이 문항은 두 단계로 판단해야 한다. 먼저 Text 1의 '태도를 거친 간접 연결' 주장을 파악하고, 다음으로 Text 2가 반례를 소개한 뒤 그것을 다시 뒤집는 구조를 따라가야 한다. 훑어 읽는 학생을 겨냥한 오답 C를 넣었고, B와 D는 Text 2의 세부 내용을 부분적으로 끌어와 만들었다.

input.passage: Linguists who study tonogenesis, the process by which a language develops tone, often point to Middle Chinese as a model case. The four tones of modern Mandarin did not arise from nowhere: they emerged as earlier consonant contrasts at the ends and beginnings of syllables, such as the voicing of initial stops, gradually ______ pitch differences that speakers had once treated as mere side effects became the primary means of distinguishing words.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: eroded, and the
eroded, the
eroded; the
eroded, and
input.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 "pitch differences ... became"는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이고, 앞의 "they emerged as earlier consonant contrasts ... gradually eroded"도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표+등위접속사로 연결해야 하며, "pitch differences"는 이미 관계절(that speakers had once treated...)의 수식을 받는 일반 복수명사라 관사 없이도 자연스럽다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표+and로 연결은 맞지만 "the pitch differences that..."가 되면 "they emerged as ... contrasts ... eroded"의 구조와 무관하게 앞에서 언급된 적 없는 특정 대상을 가리켜 어색할 뿐 아니라, 핵심 문제는 B와 C에 있다: B는 접속사 없이 쉼표만 써서 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C의 세미콜론은 두 독립절 연결 자체는 가능하지만 "emerged as contrasts ... eroded"라는 앞절 내부의 'as' 절을 끊어 'as' 절이 뒤 결과와 분리되어 의미 흐름이 무너진다. 문장부호 규칙상 가장 명확하고 표준적인 선택은 D이다.
input.explanation_en: The words after the blank, "pitch differences ... became the primary means," form an independent clause, and so does the part before it, "they emerged as earlier consonant contrasts ... gradually eroded." Two independent clauses can be joined with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so D is correct, and "pitch differences" is already specified by its "that" clause, so it needs no article. B links the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C's semicolon cuts the "as" clause off from the result it leads to, so the logic of the sentence falls apart. A adds "the," which points to specific pitch differences the text has never mentioned before. D is the cleanest, most standard choice.
input.design: 긴 동격·수식어(such as ...) 뒤에서 절 경계를 판단하게 했고, 오답은 모두 같은 'eroded+부호' 틀로 맞췄다.

input.passage: On the No. 28 tram climbing toward Alfama, Fernanda recognized the man by the crooked set of his left ear, the same as his sister Inês's. Thirty-one years earlier, at Inês's bedside, Fernanda had promised to find him and tell him he was forgiven, and in the decades since, she had rehearsed the sentence so often that she could recite it without thinking. ______ when he glanced up and met her eyes, the words would not come; she stared at her shopping bag until the tram lurched to a stop at her street.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Even so,
As a result,
In other words,
Likewise,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 페르난다가 그 문장을 수없이 연습해 생각 없이도 말할 수 있었다고 하고, 뒷문장은 정작 그를 마주하자 말이 나오지 않았다고 한다. 준비가 충분했는데도 예상과 반대 결과가 나왔으므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 연습이 말문이 막힌 원인인 것처럼 만드는데, 지문에서 연습은 오히려 쉽게 말할 수 있게 해 줄 근거로 제시되어 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. C는 뒷문장이 앞문장을 바꿔 말한 것으로 보게 하지만 두 문장의 내용은 서로 반대이다. D는 비슷한 내용을 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 말이 나오지 않은 것은 술술 외울 수 있었다는 사실과 비슷하지 않다.
input.explanation_en: The earlier sentence says Fernanda practiced the sentence so many times that she could recite it without thinking. The next sentence says that when she actually faced the man, the words would not come. She was well prepared, yet the opposite of what you'd expect happened, so this is a concession followed by a reversal, and A fits. B treats the practice as the cause of her silence, but the passage presents the practice as something that should have made speaking easy, so the cause and effect run the wrong way. C would make the second sentence a restatement of the first, but the two sentences say opposite things. D adds a similar point, but freezing up is not similar to being able to recite the words easily.
input.design: There is no "but" or "however" in the passage, so the contrast only shows up if you see that years of practice should lead to fluency, not silence. B tempts students who read the long buildup as the cause of her freezing, and C and D tempt those who see the two sentences as simply continuing the same idea.

content.text:
Passage idea: a sentence with a long nonessential modifier, followed by an independent clause boundary.

"The owl arrived on a Thursday, during brass band practice. Greta Schäfer, who had spent the eleven years since her husband's death speaking to almost no one but the grocer, opened the back door to find it hunched on the step, one wing dragging ______ she would later tell her neighbors, that was the moment her life split into before and after."

Blank after "dragging": the next part is an independent clause ("that was the moment..." with the inserted "she would later tell her neighbors,"). Hmm, the comma after "neighbors" means "she would later tell her neighbors" is a parenthetical, so the blank needs a sentence boundary. Correct answer: "dragging. As" ... no, I'm keeping it simple: the options are punctuation only. Correct: "; as she would later tell..." That changes the words, though. Alternatively, make the text after the blank "and, as she would later tell her neighbors, that was..." Options: A "dragging, and," B "dragging and," C "dragging—and," hmm.

Better: the blank precedes "as she would later tell her neighbors, that was the moment". Options: A ", as" (comma splice); B " as" (run-on); C "; as" (correct); D ", and as" with no comma after... wait, D ", and as" would actually be fine. So D should be ": as,", which is wrong because of the comma after "as". Final options: A "dragging, as", B "dragging as", C "dragging; as", D "dragging, and, as she" ... no. I'll use D "dragging; as," which wrongly splits "as" from its clause.

input.passage: The owl arrived on a Thursday evening, while the village brass band was rehearsing in the Schäfers' front parlor. Greta Schäfer, who in the eleven years since her husband's death had spoken to almost no one but the grocer, slipped out the back door to escape the noise and found the bird hunched on the step, one wing dragging in the dust______ as she would later tell her neighbors, that was the moment her life split cleanly into before and after.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; as,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Greta ... found the bird ... in the dust'는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 'as she would later tell her neighbors'는 삽입구라서 그 뒤의 'that was the moment ...'도 독립절이다. 따라서 두 독립절 사이에는 세미콜론이 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 문장부호가 전혀 없어 'as'가 앞 절에 붙는 것처럼 읽히는 run-on이 된다. D는 경계는 맞게 표시했지만 'as' 뒤에 쉼표를 넣어 'as'와 그 절('she would later tell')을 끊어 놓는다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("Greta ... found the bird ... in the dust") form an independent clause. After the blank, "as she would later tell her neighbors" is just an interrupting phrase, so "that was the moment..." is a second independent clause. Two independent clauses need a strong boundary like a semicolon, so C is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B has no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on. D marks the boundary correctly but puts a comma after "as," which cuts "as" off from the clause it introduces.
input.design: 긴 삽입절과 'as ...' 삽입구 때문에 뒤 절이 독립절임이 잘 보이지 않는다. 오답 D는 세미콜론을 맞게 쓰고도 'as'를 잘못 끊었고, A는 쉼표를 쓴 그럴듯한 오답이다.

input.passage: Giovanna had found the stranger crumpled at the foot of the tenement stairs, a bruise already darkening above one eye. Now, seated on the stoop with a bowl of her lentil soup balanced on his knees, the man who had been knocked senseless only an hour before ______ thanking her in a halting mixture of English and Neapolitan dialect. His injuries had not frightened her; it was the steadiness of his gratitude, as if no one had ever fed him before, that made her look away toward the street.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: having kept
kept
who kept
keeping
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'the man'이고, 'who had been knocked senseless only an hour before'는 주어를 꾸미는 관계절이므로 문장에는 아직 정동사가 없다. 따라서 정동사 'kept'(B)가 와야 완전한 문장이 된다. A의 'having kept'와 D의 'keeping'은 분사여서 정동사 역할을 할 수 없고, 주어만 남은 불완전한 문장이 된다. C의 'who kept'는 관계절을 하나 더 덧붙일 뿐이라 여전히 주절의 동사가 없다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "the man," and "who had been knocked senseless only an hour before" is a relative clause that modifies it, so the sentence still needs a main verb. Only the finite verb "kept" in B completes the sentence. A ("having kept") and D ("keeping") are participles, which can't act as main verbs, so they leave you with a subject and no predicate. C ("who kept") just adds a second relative clause, so the main clause still has no verb.
input.design: 긴 관계절이 주어와 빈칸을 갈라 놓아서, 훑어 읽으면 'who had been...'에 이미 동사가 있다고 착각하기 쉽다. 그래서 분사 선택지와 관계절 선택지가 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

input.passage: A quartz crystal used in a wristwatch is cut so that it vibrates at 32,768 times per second when voltage is applied, a property known as piezoelectric resonance. This frequency is not perfectly fixed, however: as temperature rises or falls, the crystal's vibration rate drifts slightly. Engineers designing precision clocks for laboratories therefore enclose the crystal in a small heated chamber that holds its temperature steady, a technique that does not remove the crystal's sensitivity to heat but ______ its effects, keeping the frequency stable enough that the clock loses less than a second over many years.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: eliminates
neutralizes
intensifies
reveals
input.explanation: 지문은 가열 챔버가 수정의 열 민감성 자체를 '없애지는 않지만' 그 영향을 막아 주파수를 안정시킨다고 말하므로, 영향을 상쇄해 무력화한다는 B(neutralizes)가 정답이다. A(eliminates)는 효과를 줄인다는 방향은 맞아 보이지만, 'does not remove ... but' 구조에서 '제거하다'는 앞 절과 같은 의미라 대조가 성립하지 않는다. C(intensifies)는 온도 변화가 영향을 준다는 점과는 연결되지만, 주파수를 안정시킨다는 결과와 반대된다. D(reveals)는 실험실 맥락에선 그럴듯하지만, 영향을 드러내는 것은 시계 안정성을 설명하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the heated chamber does not remove the crystal's sensitivity to heat, yet it keeps the frequency stable. So the chamber must cancel out the effects of that sensitivity, which makes B (neutralizes) correct. A (eliminates) points the right way, but it means the same thing as "remove," so the "does not remove ... but" contrast falls apart. C (intensifies) ties in with the idea that temperature affects the crystal, but it contradicts the stable frequency. D (reveals) sounds natural in a lab setting, but showing the effects would not explain why the clock stays accurate.
input.design: The answer depends on two clues together: the "does not remove ... but" contrast and the stability result. Each wrong choice fits only one of these clues, so a quick read could pick A.

input.passage: In many classrooms of the early 1980s, computers served mainly to drill students on arithmetic facts and to score their answers ______ Logo, the programming language that mathematician Seymour Papert helped design, children gave commands to a screen "turtle" so that it would draw shapes, teaching the machine instead of being taught by it.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , so in
, in
but in;
, but in
input.explanation: 이 문장은 독립절 두 개로 되어 있다. 앞 절은 컴퓨터가 아이들을 반복 훈련하고 채점하는 데 쓰였다는 내용이고, 뒤 절(in Logo ... children gave commands ...)은 아이들이 오히려 기계를 가르쳤다는 내용이다. 두 절은 서로 대조 관계이므로 쉼표에 대조의 등위접속사 but을 더한 D가 정답이다. A: 쉼표+등위접속사라는 구조는 맞지만, so는 인과를 나타낸다. 반복 훈련 때문에 Logo에서 아이들이 기계를 가르치게 된 것이 아니므로 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다. B: 독립절 두 개를 쉼표 하나로만 이어서 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 전치사구 'in Logo' 한가운데에 들어가 있다. 그 결과 뒤쪽은 독립절이 되지 못하고, 앞쪽도 'but in'에서 어색하게 끊긴다.
input.explanation_en: This sentence is made of two independent clauses. The first says computers were used to drill and score students. The second (in Logo ... children gave commands ...) says children taught the machine instead. These ideas contrast, so the right fix is a comma plus the contrasting conjunction "but," which is choice D. Choice A has the right structure (comma plus a coordinating conjunction), but "so" signals cause and effect. The drilling did not cause children to program the turtle, so the logic doesn't fit. Choice B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. Choice C puts the semicolon in the middle of the phrase "in Logo" instead of at the boundary between the clauses. That leaves "but in" hanging awkwardly, and what follows the semicolon is not an independent clause.
input.design: 이 문항은 대조 관계에 있는 독립절 두 개를 쓰고 정답을 ', but'으로 정했다. 오답 세 개는 각각 인과 접속사 so를 잘못 쓴 경우, 콤마 스플라이스, 전치사구 안에 세미콜론을 잘못 넣은 경우로 구성했다. 구두점 구조가 같은 A와 D 가운데 정답을 고르려면 두 절의 의미 관계까지 따져야 한다.

input.passage: Elias had paid forty dollars for the desk mostly out of pity: its legs had been splinted with mismatched pine, and a crack ran the length of its top. Back at the truck, he worked the swollen bottom drawer loose and found a bundle of envelopes tied with baling twine, each addressed in his grandfather's slanted hand to a woman named Ruth Avila ______ of them had ever been stamped.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , none
; none
none
and, none
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "he worked ... Ruth Avila"는 긴 수식어(tied with..., each addressed...)를 포함하지만 그 자체로 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "none of them had ever been stamped"도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. 앞의 쉼표 수식어들 때문에 쉼표가 자연스러워 보이지만 접속사가 없다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 and와 그것이 연결하는 절을 부당하게 분리한다.
input.explanation_en: Even with its long modifiers ("tied with baling twine," "each addressed..."), the part before the blank is still a complete independent clause, and "none of them had ever been stamped" is also an independent clause. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. The commas earlier in the sentence can make a comma look right here, but there's no conjunction. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it's a run-on sentence. D places a comma after "and," which wrongly cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.
input.design: 긴 분사구·독립분사구가 앞 절 끝에 붙어 있어 쉼표 연결이 자연스러워 보이도록 했다. 절 경계를 인식한 뒤 접속사가 있는지 확인하는 두 단계가 필요하다.

input.passage: Barium titanate ceramics are widely used in multilayer capacitors because their high dielectric constant lets them store substantial charge in a small volume. Engineers have long tried to raise that constant further by doping the ceramic with rare earth oxides such as those of dysprosium or holmium, whose ions can substitute into the crystal lattice and alter how it polarizes. __Yet early doping trials frequently produced ceramics whose dielectric constant rose at room temperature but collapsed as the capacitor warmed during operation.__ Materials scientist Keiko Arata and colleagues traced this instability to dopant ions clustering unevenly near grain boundaries. By adding the dopants in two stages during sintering, the team distributed the ions more uniformly, yielding ceramics that kept their enhanced dielectric constant across a wide temperature range.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It identifies a shortcoming of an earlier approach that the research described later in the text was designed to overcome.
It presents evidence that rare earth doping fails to raise the dielectric constant of barium titanate under any conditions.
It explains the mechanism by which dopant ions cluster near grain boundaries during sintering.
It describes the outcome of Arata's team's two-stage method for adding dopants to the ceramic.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 초기 도핑 시도가 상온에서는 유전율을 높였지만 온도가 오르면 효과가 무너졌다는 한계를 제시하고, 이어지는 Arata 팀의 연구가 바로 그 불안정성을 해결한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 '어떤 조건에서도' 실패한다고 과장하는데, 지문은 상온에서 유전율이 올랐다고 말한다. C의 결정립계 근처 이온 뭉침은 다음 문장에서 원인으로 제시되는 내용이지 밑줄 문장의 기능이 아니다. D는 마지막 문장이 설명하는 2단계 방법의 결과로, 밑줄 문장은 그 이전의 문제를 다룬다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence points out a problem with early doping trials: the dielectric constant went up at room temperature but collapsed as the capacitor heated. The rest of the text then shows how Arata's team fixed that instability, so A is correct. B overstates the claim, since the text says doping did raise the constant at room temperature. C describes the cause that the next sentence identifies, which is not the job of the underlined sentence. D matches the final sentence's result, but the underlined sentence describes the earlier problem, not the solution.
input.design: B, C, D는 각각 지문의 실제 내용(도핑 효과, 원인 기작, 해결 결과)을 다루지만 범위가 과장됐거나 다른 문장의 기능이라서, 밑줄 문장이 글 전체에서 어디에 놓이는지 확인해야만 배제할 수 있다.

input.passage: In March 1871, after France's defeat in the Franco-Prussian War, the national government under Adolphe Thiers tried to remove cannons held by the Paris National Guard. Parisians resisted, and the city soon elected its own council, the Commune. Many historians have described the Commune mainly as a doomed military revolt, pointing to its brutal suppression by government troops during the "Bloody Week" of late May. Historian Carolyn Eichner, however, argues that this focus hides much of what the Commune actually did. During its roughly ten weeks in power, the council banned night work in bakeries, turned workshops abandoned by their owners over to workers' cooperatives, and separated church from state. Women's groups organized cooperative workshops and pushed for equal pay for teachers. For Eichner, these measures show that the Commune was an attempt to rebuild everyday social and economic life, not simply an armed standoff that ended in defeat.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although the Commune passed many reforms, its violent defeat during the Bloody Week shows that its leaders cared more about fighting than about governing.
One historian contends that the Commune's short-lived policies on work, religion, and equality show it was more than the failed armed revolt that many accounts describe.
Women's organizations were the main force behind the Commune, and historians have ignored their role because they focus on military events.
The Commune began when Parisians resisted the Thiers government's attempt to seize cannons, which led directly to the city's suppression in May.
input.explanation: 지문은 코뮌을 실패한 군사 반란으로만 보는 기존 시각과, 노동·종교·평등 관련 정책을 근거로 코뮌이 일상생활 재건 시도였다는 Eichner의 주장을 대비시키므로 B가 정답이다. A는 개혁과 진압을 모두 언급하지만, 지도자들이 통치보다 전투를 중시했다는 결론은 지문의 주장과 정반대이다. C는 여성 단체를 다루기는 하나, 그들은 여러 사례 중 하나일 뿐이며 '주된 세력'이라는 말은 지문에 없다. D는 사실 배경을 정확히 요약하지만 지문의 중심 논지인 Eichner의 재해석을 빠뜨렸다.
input.explanation_en: The text contrasts the common view of the Commune as a doomed military revolt with Eichner's argument, which uses its labor, religious, and equality reforms to show it was an effort to rebuild everyday life, so B is correct. A mentions both the reforms and the suppression, but its claim that the leaders cared more about fighting than governing is the opposite of the text's point. C picks up on the women's groups, but the text gives them as only one example among several and never calls them the main force. D gets the background facts right, but it leaves out the central idea, which is Eichner's reinterpretation.
input.design: Medium difficulty: the reader has to link the conventional view to Eichner's counterargument and her evidence. A and C reuse real details from the text but distort them, and D is an accurate summary of background details only.

input.passage: In the early 1900s, many American critics treated ragtime as disposable entertainment—music for saloons and dance halls, unworthy of comparison with the European concert tradition. Scott Joplin's piano rags complicate that judgment. His "Maple Leaf Rag" (1899) follows a carefully balanced multi-strain design, with each sixteen-measure section returning and contrasting in a plan as deliberate as that of a classical march or rondo. __Joplin himself printed a warning on several of his scores that ragtime should never be played fast, insisting that the syncopations needed a measured tempo to be heard clearly.__ That instruction suggests that Joplin regarded his rags not as improvised novelties but as fixed compositions whose structure performers were obligated to respect—precisely the attitude critics reserved for "serious" music.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a performance practice that critics cited as proof that ragtime was mere dance-hall entertainment.
It presents a detail about Joplin's scores that the text then uses to support a claim about how he viewed his own work.
It introduces a technical feature of ragtime's form that the text then compares with the structure of classical marches.
It offers evidence that Joplin's rags were more difficult to perform than the classical works favored by critics.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 Joplin이 악보에 '빠르게 치지 말라'는 지시를 적었다는 세부 사실을 제시하고, 다음 문장이 'That instruction'으로 그것을 받아 Joplin이 자기 래그를 존중받아야 할 고정된 작품으로 여겼다는 주장의 근거로 삼으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 비평가들이 래그타임을 깎아내렸다는 내용은 지문에 있지만, 그들이 이 연주 관행을 근거로 들었다는 말은 없다. C는 고전 행진곡과의 비교가 지문에 나오기는 하지만 그 비교는 밑줄 앞 문장에서 이루어지며, 밑줄 문장은 형식이 아니라 템포 지시를 다룬다. D는 연주의 난이도를 비교한 적이 없으므로 지문 범위를 넘어선다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence gives a specific detail: Joplin printed a warning on his scores not to play ragtime fast. The next sentence picks it up with "That instruction" and uses it as evidence that Joplin saw his rags as fixed compositions that deserved respect, so B is correct. A is wrong because the text does say critics looked down on ragtime, but it never says they pointed to this performance practice as proof. C is wrong because the comparison with classical marches does appear, but it comes in the sentence before the underlined one, and the underlined sentence is about a tempo instruction, not form. D is wrong because the text never compares how hard Joplin's rags are to play with classical works.
input.design: 오답 A와 C에는 지문에 실제로 나오는 요소(비평가들의 경멸, 행진곡과의 비교)를 넣어서, 밑줄 문장과 바로 다음 문장이 어떻게 이어지는지를 확인해야만 배제되게 했다. 질문에는 정답의 핵심어(view, support)를 쓰지 않았다.

input.passage: When a liquid such as water is exposed to intense sound waves, tiny gas bubbles form, swell during the low-pressure phase of each wave, and then collapse violently during the high-pressure phase. In a phenomenon called sonoluminescence, each collapse is accompanied by a flash of light lasting less than a billionth of a second. Researchers have long agreed that the collapse squeezes the bubble's contents and heats them intensely, but the source of the light itself remains disputed. Some physicists propose that the gas becomes so hot that it ionizes into a plasma that glows; others argue that the light comes from chemical reactions among molecules broken apart by the compression. Experiments by Seth Putterman and colleagues found that adding small amounts of noble gases such as argon to the bubbles greatly brightens the flashes, a result consistent with more than one of these explanations. As a result, although measurements of the flashes have become increasingly precise, they have not yet settled which process produces the glow.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Scientists generally accept that collapsing bubbles heat their contents, but the specific process that generates sonoluminescent light is still unresolved.
Scientists generally accept that adding noble gases to bubbles brightens sonoluminescent flashes, which shows that the light comes from a glowing plasma.
Scientists generally accept that sonoluminescent flashes are too brief to measure precisely, which has kept researchers from studying how bubbles collapse.
Scientists generally accept that chemical reactions, rather than heating, cause bubbles in liquids to collapse during the high-pressure phase of sound waves.
input.explanation: 지문은 기포 붕괴가 내부 기체를 가열한다는 점에는 합의가 있지만 빛의 근원(플라스마 대 화학 반응)은 여전히 논쟁 중이라는 점을 중심으로 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 아르곤 실험을 언급하지만, 지문은 그 결과가 여러 설명과 모두 맞아떨어진다고 했으므로 플라스마설을 입증한다는 결론은 틀렸다. C는 섬광이 매우 짧다는 세부 사항을 활용하지만, 지문은 측정이 점점 더 정밀해졌다고 말한다. D는 화학 반응을 빛의 원인 후보가 아니라 기포 붕괴의 원인으로 잘못 연결했으며, 지문에서 붕괴는 고압 단계 때문에 일어난다.
input.explanation_en: Choice A is correct because the text says researchers agree that the collapse heats the bubble's contents, while the source of the light (a glowing plasma or chemical reactions) is still disputed. Choice B mentions the argon experiment, but the text says that result is consistent with more than one explanation, so it doesn't prove the plasma idea. Choice C picks up on how brief the flashes are, but the text actually says measurements have become increasingly precise. Choice D gets the role of chemical reactions wrong: in the text, they are a possible source of the light, not the cause of the collapse, which happens because of the high-pressure phase of the sound wave.
input.design: 세부 정보(아르곤 실험, 섬광 지속 시간, 화학 반응)를 오답 근거로 쓰고, 정답은 '합의 대 미해결'이라는 구조를 파악해야 고를 수 있게 했다. 네 선택지 모두 같은 문장 틀을 사용했다.

input.passage: In a 1968 study, psychologists John Darley and Bibb Latané had college students talk over an intercom with peers they believed were in other rooms. Partway through, one voice appeared to have a seizure. Participants who thought they were the only other listener almost always left their rooms to get help, and they usually did so quickly. Those who believed four other people were also listening responded less often and more slowly. Notably, the researchers did not find these hesitant participants indifferent: many were sweating and trembling, and they repeatedly asked whether someone was helping. Darley and Latané concluded that the presence of others does not make bystanders stop caring. Instead, it spreads the sense of obligation across the group, so each person feels less personally responsible for acting.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Darley and Latané found that participants who believed they were alone with the victim felt more distress than those who believed others were listening.
Darley and Latané found that participants in larger groups were less concerned about the victim because they assumed the seizure was not serious.
Darley and Latané found that hearing about other listeners made participants slower to act not because it reduced concern but because it weakened each person's sense of duty to respond.
Darley and Latané found that participants who used an intercom were less willing to help than people who see an emergency in person usually are.
input.explanation: C가 정답이다. 지문은 다른 청취자가 있다고 믿은 참가자가 늦게 반응했지만 땀을 흘리고 떨 만큼 걱정했다고 하며, 그 원인을 관심 부족이 아닌 책임감 분산으로 결론짓는다. A는 혼자인 참가자가 더 빨리 도왔다는 사실과 연결되지만, 지문은 집단 조건 참가자도 심한 고통을 보였다고 하므로 고통의 크기를 비교한 내용이 아니다. B는 집단에서 반응이 줄었다는 점은 맞지만, 관심이 적었다는 설명은 저자들의 결론과 정면으로 어긋나고 발작이 심각하지 않다고 여겼다는 언급도 없다. D는 인터콤 사용에서 나온 그럴듯한 추론이지만, 지문에는 직접 목격한 경우와의 비교가 없다.
input.explanation_en: C is correct. The text says participants who believed others were listening responded more slowly, yet they were sweating, trembling, and asking whether anyone was helping. The researchers concluded that the cause was a spread-out sense of responsibility, not a lack of caring. A ties to the fact that participants who thought they were alone helped faster, but the text says the group participants were also clearly distressed, so it never compares how much distress each group felt. B gets right that the groups responded less, but saying those participants cared less contradicts the researchers' conclusion, and the text never says anyone thought the seizure wasn't serious. D is a reasonable guess based on the intercom setup, but the text never compares the study to emergencies people see in person.
input.design: To get the answer, you have to connect the slower responses with the evidence that the hesitant participants were distressed. A quick read might suggest they didn't care (B) or that the two groups differed in distress (A).

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Breaker Room is a 2019 novel by South Korean writer Han Ji-woo.
- Its main character, Min, is a 28-year-old accountant who labels every drawer and shelf in her Seoul apartment.
- In the novel's central scene, a citywide blackout leaves Min's apartment complex dark for six hours.
- Searching for candles by touch, Min opens an unlabeled box that she had taped shut years earlier.
- The box holds letters from an older brother whom Min has told her coworkers she never had.
- Reviewers have praised Han's spare, precise prose.
input.question: The student wants to explain how the novel's central scene upsets the main character's carefully arranged life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In The Breaker Room, a 2019 novel by South Korean writer Han Ji-woo, Min is a 28-year-old accountant living in Seoul, and reviewers have praised the novel's spare, precise prose.
In The Breaker Room, Min is an accountant who labels every drawer and shelf in her Seoul apartment, a habit that Han Ji-woo describes in spare, precise prose.
In The Breaker Room, Min keeps a taped box of letters from an older brother, though she has told her coworkers that she never had a brother.

In The Breaker Room, Min, who labels every drawer and shelf she owns, must search by touch during a blackout and ends up opening a long-sealed, unlabeled box of letters from a brother she has denied having.
input.explanation: 목표는 중심 장면이 Min의 정돈된 삶을 어떻게 흔드는지 설명하는 것이므로, Min의 정돈 습관(라벨)과 정전 장면, 그리고 그 결과 드러나는 숨긴 과거를 함께 연결해야 한다. D는 이 세 요소를 모두 결합해 정답이다. A는 작품 기본 정보와 문체 평가만 제시하고 중심 장면은 다루지 않는다. B는 Min의 정돈 습관은 언급하지만 그것이 흔들리는 장면이 없다. C는 숨긴 과거(편지)는 언급하지만 정전 장면과 정돈된 삶과의 대비가 빠져 있다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how the central scene upsets Min's carefully arranged life, so you need to connect three things: her orderly habits (the labels), the blackout scene, and the hidden past it exposes. D combines all three, so it's the correct answer. A gives only basic facts about the novel and a comment on its prose; it never mentions the central scene. B describes Min's labeling habit but leaves out the scene that disrupts it. C mentions the hidden letters but not the blackout, and it doesn't contrast them with her orderly life.
input.design: To get this right, you have to link the note about her orderly habits with the blackout and box notes. Each wrong choice uses accurate notes but covers only one part of the goal, so you can't eliminate them without comparing. The question avoids the answer's key words (labels, blackout, box).

input.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story.

At dawn, Linh found the envelope wedged beneath her door in the narrow Hanoi alley, its paper gone soft as cloth from the long journey north from Hue. Her husband's brother had not written in twenty years, not since the quarrel at the funeral, and his letter never mentioned it: he described the late monsoon, the price of rice, the ache that had settled in his left knee. ______ each page closed with the same small question—whether the persimmon tree their mother had planted beside the alley gate still bore fruit—and Linh understood that he was asking, as carefully as he could, whether anything between them had survived.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Yet,
Likewise,
Consequently,
For instance,
input.explanation:
정답 A(Yet,): 앞 문장은 편지가 장마, 쌀값, 무릎 통증 같은 평범한 이야기만 하고 다툼은 꺼내지 않는다는 표면적 내용이다. 마지막 문장은 그 평범함 밑에 깔린 숨은 의도, 즉 관계가 아직 남아 있는지 조심스럽게 묻는 마음을 드러낸다. 표면과 의도가 대조되므로 역접 'Yet'이 맞다.
B(Likewise,): 감나무 질문도 날씨나 쌀값처럼 집안의 사소한 이야기로 보면 그럴듯하다. 하지만 이 문장의 핵심은 그 질문이 앞의 화제들과 '다르게' 숨은 의미를 품고 있다는 점이므로 유사 관계는 강조점에서 벗어난다.
C(Consequently,): 다툼을 피했기 때문에 돌려서 물었다는 인과로 읽을 수도 있어 방향은 비슷해 보인다. 그러나 마지막 문장은 앞 문장에서 생긴 결과가 아니다. 사소한 내용과 진심 어린 질문 사이의 대비를 보여 주는 문장이다.
D(For instance,): 마지막 문장은 날씨, 쌀값, 무릎 통증 같은 일상 묘사의 예시가 아니다. 그래서 앞 내용과 연결되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is A, "Yet." The sentence before the blank tells you what the letter says on the surface. It covers ordinary things like the monsoon, rice prices, and a sore knee, and it never mentions the quarrel. The last sentence shows the hidden purpose under all that ordinary talk: the brother is carefully asking whether their relationship survived. The surface content and the real intent are in contrast, so you need a contrast word like "Yet."
B, "Likewise," is wrong. You might treat the persimmon question as one more household detail like the weather. But the point of the sentence is that this question is different from those topics because it carries a deeper meaning.
C, "Consequently," is wrong. You could guess that he asked indirectly because he avoided the quarrel, but the last sentence isn't a result of the one before it. It sets the trivial details against the heartfelt question.
D, "For instance," is wrong because the last sentence isn't an example of the everyday details about weather, rice, and his knee.
input.design: 이 문항은 평범한 화제를 여러 개 나열해 두고, 그 표면 내용과 숨은 의도의 대비 하나만 정답과 직결되게 만들었다. 오답은 세 유형이다. Likewise는 부수적 화제와 표면이 일치하는 함정이고, Consequently는 방향은 비슷하지만 인과로 관계를 잘못 읽은 경우이며, For instance는 내용과 관계없는 연결어이다.

input.passage: Early tissue-engineering scaffolds were cast as solid polymer blocks with smooth, flat surfaces. Electrospun scaffolds, in contrast, are mats of polymer fibers only a few hundred nanometers wide, matching the scale of the collagen fibrils in natural tissue rather than that of the blocks' broad surfaces. ______ cells seeded on the electrospun mats attach, spread, and multiply in patterns resembling those seen in the body.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
Even so,
Instead,
Consequently,
input.explanation:
두 번째 문장 끝의 "rather than that of the blocks' broad surfaces"에서 "that"은 바로 앞의 collagen fibrils가 아니라 문장 주어인 전기방사 섬유(fibers)의 '크기'를 가리킨다. 즉 이 문장의 요지는 '섬유가 천연 조직의 콜라겐 섬유와 같은 크기다'라는 것이다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 세포가 몸속과 비슷하게 자란다는 내용이므로 인과의 'Consequently,'(D)가 정답이다.
A(Similarly): 바로 옆 명사인 collagen fibrils를 독립된 비교 대상으로 보고 세포의 행동을 그것과 나란히 놓은 오답이다. 그러나 콜라겐 섬유는 섬유 크기를 재는 기준일 뿐 세포 행동과 병렬되는 사례가 아니다.
B(Even so): 'in contrast', 'rather than' 같은 대조 표현에 끌려 양보로 읽은 오답이다. 문법적으로는 자연스럽지만, 섬유 크기가 조직과 닮았다는 사실은 좋은 세포 성장을 뒷받침하므로 양보 관계가 성립하지 않는다.
C(Instead): 지시 대상을 첫 문장의 고분자 블록으로 잡고 '블록 대신'이라는 대체 관계로 읽은 오답이다. 그러나 빈칸 뒤 문장은 앞 문장에서 이어지는 결과를 말할 뿐, 블록에 대한 진술을 대체하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
In the second sentence, "that" in "rather than that of the blocks' broad surfaces" doesn't point to the nearby noun "collagen fibrils." It points back to the scale of the electrospun fibers, which are the sentence's subject. So the sentence's main claim is that the fibers match the scale of natural collagen fibrils. The next sentence says cells on these mats grow the way they do in the body, which is a result of that match. That makes "Consequently," (D) the answer.
A ("Similarly,") treats the nearby "collagen fibrils" as a separate item that the cells' behavior is being compared to. But the fibrils are only the size reference for the fibers, not a parallel example.
B ("Even so,") comes from being pulled in by the contrast words "in contrast" and "rather than." It sounds fine grammatically, but the fibers matching tissue scale supports good cell growth instead of working against it, so a concession doesn't fit.
C ("Instead,") takes the blocks from the first sentence as the reference point and reads the last sentence as a replacement. In fact, the last sentence states a result that follows from the fiber scale.
input.design: "that of the blocks"의 that은 인접 명사 fibrils가 아니라 주어인 fibers의 크기를 가리키도록 했다. 이 지시 관계를 제대로 잡아야 결과 관계가 보인다. 오답은 각각 인접 명사를 지시 대상으로 본 경우(Similarly), 대조어에 끌린 경우(Even so), 첫 문장의 블록을 지시 대상으로 삼은 경우(Instead)에 대응한다.

input.passage: When a large volcano erupts, it can send sulfur dioxide gas high into the stratosphere. There, the gas reacts with water to form tiny droplets called sulfate aerosols, which reflect some incoming sunlight back into space. To track this effect, scientists measure stratospheric optical depth, a number that shows how much the aerosol layer dims sunlight passing through it. __For example, after Mount Pinatubo erupted in the Philippines in 1991, optical depth readings rose sharply, and average global temperatures fell by about half a degree Celsius over the next year.__ Measurements like these help researchers predict how strongly future eruptions might cool the planet.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives a specific case that illustrates the process described earlier in the text.
It gives a specific case that challenges the process described earlier in the text.
It gives a specific case that explains why scientists stopped measuring optical depth.
It gives a specific case that introduces the main topic of the text for the first time.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'For example'로 시작하며, 앞에서 설명한 과정(황산염 에어로졸이 햇빛을 반사해 냉각을 일으키고 광학 깊이로 측정됨)의 실제 사례로 피나투보 화산을 제시한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 틀렸다. 이 사례는 앞의 설명을 반박하지 않고 뒷받침한다. C도 틀렸다. 지문 마지막 문장은 이런 측정이 계속 유용하다고 말하므로 측정을 그만둔 이유가 아니다. D도 틀렸다. 주제는 이미 첫 문장들에서 소개되었다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "For example." It uses the Mount Pinatubo eruption as a real case of the process explained earlier: sulfate aerosols reflect sunlight and cause cooling, and scientists measure this with optical depth. That makes A correct. B is wrong because the example supports the earlier explanation instead of challenging it. C is wrong because the last sentence says these measurements are still useful, so the example isn't about why scientists stopped measuring. D is wrong because the first sentences already introduced the topic.
input.design: 'For example'라는 명시적 신호어 하나로 예시 기능을 파악하게 하는 easy 문항으로 설계했다. 오답들은 정답과 같은 'It gives a specific case that…' 틀을 쓰되 반박, 측정 중단, 주제 첫 소개라는 흔한 오해를 담았다.

input.passage: Polish-German thinker Rosa Luxemburg refused to separate theory from action. In essays such as "Reform or Revolution," she argued that philosophical ideas about society mattered only when tested in real political struggle. She did not write from a distant library ______ she wrote while organizing workers, editing newspapers, and even serving time in prison.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: library,
library
library;
library, and,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "She did not write from a distant library"와 빈칸 뒤 "she wrote while organizing workers..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 연결하려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었을 뿐 아니라, and는 두 절의 대조 관계에도 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "She did not write from a distant library," and the text after it, "she wrote while organizing workers...," are both independent clauses, since each has its own subject and verb. When two independent clauses are joined without a conjunction, you need a semicolon, so C is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence. D adds an unneeded comma after the conjunction "and," and "and" also doesn't fit the contrast between the two clauses.
input.design: 독립절 두 개가 접속사 없이 맞닿은 경계를 두고 세미콜론 하나만 알면 풀리게 했다. 오답에는 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 접속사에 붙은 잘못된 쉼표라는 흔한 오개념을 넣었다.

input.passage: When titanium dioxide nanoparticles absorb ultraviolet light, they generate highly reactive hydroxyl radicals that attack the large, colored molecules of textile dyes such as methylene blue. Chemist Lena Okafor and her team found, however, that the radicals do not destroy a dye molecule in a single step. Instead, they ______ it gradually, first severing the bonds responsible for its color and then breaking the remaining fragments into progressively smaller compounds until only carbon dioxide, water, and simple mineral ions remain.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: dilute
conceal
absorb
dismantle
input.explanation: 지문은 라디칼이 염료 분자의 결합을 끊고 조각을 점점 더 작은 화합물로 쪼개는 단계적 분해 과정을 설명하므로, 구조를 하나씩 해체한다는 뜻의 D가 정확하다. A는 색이 옅어진다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 농도를 낮추는 것일 뿐 분자를 쪼개는 것이 아니다. B는 색이 사라지는 현상과 연결되지만, 분자가 숨겨지는 것이 아니라 실제로 파괴된다. C는 나노입자가 빛을 흡수한다는 앞 문장과 겹치지만, 라디칼이 염료에 하는 일인 결합 절단과는 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the radicals sever bonds and break fragments into progressively smaller compounds, which is step-by-step taking apart of a structure, so D is the most precise choice. A may seem plausible because the color fades, but diluting only lowers concentration and does not break molecules apart. B connects to the loss of color, but the dye is actually destroyed, not hidden. C echoes the earlier mention of nanoparticles absorbing light, but absorbing does not describe the radicals cutting bonds in the dye.
input.design: 오답 A·B는 '색이 사라짐'이라는 부분 근거, C는 앞 문장의 '흡수'와 표면적으로 연결되게 하여, '단계적으로 결합을 끊어 쪼갠다'는 뒷부분을 정독해야 D를 고를 수 있게 했다.

content.text:
Easy 문항: 짧은 수식어가 있는 주어-동사 수 일치 또는 시제 일관성. 과거 시제 서사에서 시제 일관성으로 하자.

Passage: "Every evening after the last ferry departed, Nikos wiped down the counter of his kiosk and set out a worn deck of cards. His opponent, a retired schoolteacher named Eleni, ______ at the same plastic table she had claimed since June. As the summer crowds thinned, the stakes grew: first a bottle of lemonade, then a week of free coffee, and finally the kiosk's faded umbrella."

Options: A sits, B will sit, C sat, D is sitting. 정답 C.

input.passage: Every evening after the last ferry departed, Nikos wiped down the counter of his kiosk and set out a worn deck of cards. His opponent, a retired schoolteacher named Eleni, ______ at the same plastic table she had claimed since June. As the summer crowds thinned, the stakes grew: first a bottle of lemonade, then a week of free coffee, and finally the kiosk's faded umbrella.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: sits
will sit
sat
is sitting
input.explanation: 이 장면은 departed, wiped, set, had claimed, thinned, grew처럼 과거 시제로 서술된다. 따라서 빈칸에도 과거형 동사 C(sat)가 와야 시제가 일관된다. A(sits)와 D(is sitting)는 현재 시제라서 과거 서사의 흐름과 어긋난다. B(will sit)는 미래 시제라서 이미 일어난 장면을 묘사하는 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: This scene is told in the past tense: departed, wiped, set, had claimed, thinned, and grew. So the blank also needs a past-tense verb, and C (sat) keeps the tense consistent. A (sits) and D (is sitting) are present tense, so they break the past-tense flow of the story. B (will sit) is future tense, which doesn't fit a scene that has already happened.
input.design: 이 문항은 시제 일관성이라는 규칙 하나만 묻는다. 지문 곳곳에 과거형 동사가 단서로 직접 드러나 있다. 오답은 같은 동사의 현재형, 미래형, 현재진행형으로 구성했다.

input.passage: In 1942, the film actress Hedy Lamarr and the composer George Antheil received a U.S. patent for a "secret communication system" designed to keep radio-guided torpedoes from being jammed. Their idea was to have the transmitter and receiver switch rapidly among 88 frequencies in a synchronized pattern, so that an enemy listening on any single channel would hear only fragments. The U.S. Navy shelved the proposal, and the patent expired before Lamarr earned anything from it. Many popular accounts now credit her with inventing the technology behind Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, but historians of engineering offer a more qualified view. Frequency hopping had been described by other inventors decades earlier, and the systems that later became widespread relied on electronic components and coding methods that did not exist in 1942. What distinguishes the Lamarr-Antheil patent, these historians argue, is its clear and practical scheme for synchronization, which helped bring the concept to the attention of military engineers in the years that followed.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although Lamarr did not originate frequency hopping or directly create modern wireless systems, her patent made a real contribution through its workable approach to coordinating signals.
Although Lamarr's patent was ignored by the Navy, it was the first design to describe switching among frequencies to protect radio signals from interference.
Although popular accounts exaggerate Lamarr's role, her patent contained the electronic components and coding methods that later made Wi-Fi and Bluetooth possible.
Although Lamarr received a patent for her invention, historians consider it insignificant because the Navy never used it and she never profited from it.
input.explanation: 지문은 라마르가 와이파이를 발명했다는 대중적 주장을 바로잡으면서도, 동기화 방식을 실용적으로 제시했다는 점을 그녀 특허의 고유한 기여로 인정한다. A가 이 두 측면을 모두 담고 있다. B는 해군이 특허를 묵살했다는 내용은 맞지만, 주파수 도약은 수십 년 전에 이미 다른 발명가들이 설명했으므로 '최초'라는 말이 지문과 모순된다. C는 과장을 지적한 부분은 맞지만, 그런 전자 부품과 부호화 방식은 1942년에 존재하지 않았다고 지문에 나온다. D는 해군이 쓰지 않았고 그녀가 수익을 얻지 못했다는 사실은 맞지만, 역사가들은 그 특허를 하찮게 여기지 않고 오히려 그 가치를 강조한다.
input.explanation_en: The text corrects the popular claim that Lamarr invented Wi-Fi, but it still credits her patent with something of its own: a practical way to synchronize signals. Choice A captures both sides of that point. Choice B gets the Navy shelving the patent right, but it calls the design "the first," which goes against the text: other inventors had described frequency hopping decades earlier. Choice C gets the exaggeration right, but the text says those components and coding methods did not exist in 1942. Choice D gets the facts about the Navy and profit right, but historians don't call the patent insignificant. They point out what made it valuable.
input.design: Every choice uses the same "Although X, Y" frame. B, C, and D each start from an accurate detail in the text but end with a false conclusion, so you have to read the whole text, including its qualified final judgment, to rule them out.

input.passage: For eleven autumns, Ramón and Diego had carried their squash to the village plaza, each certain the judges would finally favor his. This year a late frost forced them to share a single greenhouse, and on the third cold night Diego broke the silence. His father, a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor ______ taught him to pinch off the first blossoms so that the vines would send their strength into the roots. Ramón listened, then knelt and showed Diego the crushed eggshells his own father had buried beneath every seedling.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; had
— had
, had
had
input.explanation: "a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor"는 주어 "His father"를 설명하는 비필수 동격어구로, 앞에 쉼표가 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 하고 그 뒤에 동사 "had taught"가 이어진다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론을 써서 주어와 동사를 갈라놓고, 세미콜론 앞부분은 독립절이 아니다. B는 대시로 닫아 쉼표로 연 동격어구와 문장부호가 맞지 않는다. D는 닫는 문장부호가 없어서 삽입 어구가 어디서 끝나는지 표시되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject "His father." It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma before the verb "had taught" continues the sentence. That makes C correct. A uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb, and the words before the semicolon don't form an independent clause. B closes with a dash, which doesn't match the comma that opened the appositive. D leaves out the closing punctuation entirely, so the reader can't tell where the inserted phrase ends.
input.design: The appositive comes between the subject and the verb, so you have to find the opening comma and then match it at the close. The semicolon and dash options can look like they mark a boundary, so you need to check them against that opening comma to rule them out.

input.passage: Code-switching, the alternation between two languages within a single conversation, was once dismissed as a sign that bilingual speakers lacked full command of either language. Sociolinguist Mariam Osei has challenged that view. Having recorded more than 300 hours of casual conversation among Twi-English bilingual teenagers in South London, ______ that the speakers' switches into Twi clustered at moments when they were asserting loyalty to friends or distancing themselves from teachers, suggesting that the practice functions as a deliberate tool for negotiating social identity.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the neighborhood's secondary schools reported
Osei's published study revealed
Osei found
the teenagers themselves noticed
input.explanation: 분사구문 'Having recorded more than 300 hours of ... conversation'은 녹음을 한 행위자를 주어로 가져야 한다. 녹음을 한 사람은 연구자 Osei이므로 'Osei found'(C)가 정답이다. A: 지역 학교들은 녹음 행위와 아무 관계없는 엉뚱한 주어로, 현수 수식어가 된다. B: 'Osei's published study'는 Osei와 관련은 있지만 사람이 아닌 저작물이다. 연구 결과물이 직접 300시간을 녹음할 수는 없으므로 수식 대상이 맞지 않는다. D: 'the teenagers'는 복수 주어와 'noticed'가 문법적으로 잘 맞고 지문에도 나오는 명사이지만, 이들은 녹음된 대상이지 녹음한 사람이 아니다. 따라서 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없다.
input.explanation_en: The sentence begins with the participial phrase "Having recorded more than 300 hours of casual conversation...". Whatever comes right after the comma has to be the one who did the recording. That was the researcher, Osei, so "Osei found" (C) is correct. A is wrong because the neighborhood's schools have nothing to do with the recording, which leaves the modifier dangling. B names something closely tied to Osei, her published study, but a study is a written work, not a person. A study can't record conversations. D uses a plural subject that agrees with its verb and appears in the passage. However, the teenagers were the people being recorded, not the ones doing the recording, so the modifier can't logically describe them.
input.design: 문장이 'Having recorded' 분사구문으로 시작하고, 네 선택지 모두 '주어+동사'로 문법적으로 완전한 같은 틀을 갖추게 했다. 오답은 각각 무관한 명사(학교), 관련은 있지만 범주가 다른 저작물(study), 수일치는 맞지만 녹음된 대상(teenagers)으로 만들어, 의미상 연결만으로 정답을 가려내게 했다.

input.passage: Common vampire bats (Desmodus rotundus) feed only on blood, so they must find spots on a sleeping animal where blood vessels lie close to the skin. Researchers have long known that pits around the bat's nose leaf can detect infrared radiation, the heat given off by warm bodies. In 2011, Elena Gracheva and her colleagues found the molecular basis for this ability: in nerve cells serving the nose leaf, the bats make a shortened form of the protein TRPV1, which in most mammals responds only to painfully high temperatures. __The shortened form, however, switches on at about 30°C, close to the temperature of skin lying over a blood vessel.__ This tuning lets the bat sense, from roughly 20 centimeters away, which patches of skin are warmest and therefore the best places to bite.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that challenges Gracheva's team's view of how the nose leaf pits detect heat.
It explains how a change in a protein makes it suited to the bat's way of locating food.
It describes a feature of a protein that vampire bats share with most other mammals.
It gives a measurement showing how far away the bat can be when it detects a warm body.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 짧아진 TRPV1이 약 30°C에서 반응한다고 말하며, 이는 혈관 위 피부 온도와 맞아 흡혈 부위를 찾는 데 적합함을 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 'however'를 연구팀 견해에 대한 반박으로 오해한 것으로, 실제로는 일반 포유류의 TRPV1과 대비할 뿐 연구 결과를 뒷받침한다. C는 정반대로, 다른 포유류의 TRPV1은 높은 온도에서만 반응한다고 했다. D의 거리(20센티미터)는 다음 문장의 정보이며, 밑줄 문장의 수치는 거리가 아니라 온도이다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence says the shortened TRPV1 switches on at about 30°C, which is close to the temperature of skin over a blood vessel. That explains why the altered protein suits the bat's way of finding a blood meal, so B is correct. A misreads "however": the word contrasts the bat's protein with the version in most other mammals, and it supports Gracheva's team's findings rather than challenging them. C is the opposite of what the text says, because in most mammals TRPV1 responds only to painfully high temperatures. D mixes up the details: the 20-centimeter distance comes in the next sentence, and the number in the underlined sentence is a temperature, not a distance.
input.design: To answer, students have to link the 30°C threshold to the temperature of skin over blood vessels, and also see that "however" sets up a contrast with other mammals. A and D draw on details from nearby sentences that are only partly relevant.

input.passage: By the time the 8:15 ferry pulled away from the pier, Odile's accordion, still strapped into the battered luggage cart she had left beside the ticket booth for only a moment, was sailing toward the wrong island. The passengers who found it ______ the case open and began coaxing out wheezing, uneven chords, and by the time the boat docked, half the deck was dancing to a song nobody could quite keep in time.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: it, unlatched,
it; unlatched
it, they unlatched
it unlatched
input.explanation: "who found it"는 어떤 승객인지 특정하는 필수 관계절이므로 쉼표로 분리하지 않으며, 주어 "The passengers"와 동사 "unlatched" 사이에도 문장부호를 두지 않으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 동사 "unlatched"를 쉼표로 감싸 삽입어처럼 만들어 주어와 동사, 동사와 목적어를 부당하게 끊는다. B는 세미콜론 앞부분 "The passengers who found it"이 동사가 없는 불완전한 절이라 쓸 수 없다. C는 주어 "The passengers"가 이미 있는데 "they"를 다시 넣어 주어가 중복되고, 앞부분이 문장 구조에서 떨어져 나간다.
input.explanation_en: The clause "who found it" tells us which passengers are meant, so it is essential and takes no commas. No punctuation should come between the subject "The passengers" and its verb "unlatched" either, so D is correct. A puts commas around the verb "unlatched," which treats it like an aside and breaks the link between the subject, the verb, and its object. B puts a semicolon after "The passengers who found it," but that part has no main verb, so it isn't an independent clause. C adds "they" even though the sentence already has the subject "The passengers," so the subject is doubled and the opening phrase is left disconnected.
input.design: 긴 관계절 뒤에서 주어-동사 경계를 판단하게 하고, 쉼표·세미콜론·주어 중복 오답이 각각 그럴듯한 절 경계처럼 보이도록 구성했다.

input.passage: Karst landscapes, marked by sinkholes, disappearing streams, and extensive caves, form where slightly acidic groundwater slowly dissolves limestone bedrock. Geologists long assumed that the largest cave passages in such regions grew mainly where water first entered the rock, since rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide from soil and is most corrosive at the surface. Yet hydrogeologist Lena Okafor noticed that in several Appalachian cave systems, the widest passages lie deep underground, far from any entry point, where incoming water should already have lost most of its dissolving power. Her sampling showed that at these depths, two separate streams of groundwater, each nearly saturated with dissolved limestone, often meet. When waters with different chemical compositions mix, the blend can become undersaturated again and regain its capacity to dissolve rock, even though neither stream could do so alone. Okafor concluded that such mixing zones, rather than surface entry points, may account for much of the large-scale enlargement of these caves.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Rainwater dissolves limestone most effectively near the surface because it absorbs carbon dioxide from soil, which explains why the widest cave passages in Appalachian karst begin at entry points.
Groundwater that becomes nearly saturated with dissolved limestone loses its ability to enlarge caves, which explains why deep passages in Appalachian karst remain narrow.
Sinkholes and disappearing streams in Appalachian karst are formed by mixing groundwater, which explains why these surface features cluster far from cave entrances.
Deep Appalachian cave passages may have been widened chiefly where two chemically different groundwater streams merge, which explains why the largest passages lie far from entry points.
input.explanation: 지문은 기존 가정(표면 진입부에서 동굴이 가장 커진다)을 소개한 뒤, Okafor가 깊은 곳에서 거의 포화된 두 지하수가 섞이면 다시 용해력을 얻는다는 점을 근거로 혼합 지대가 대형 통로 확장의 주원인일 수 있다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하는 기존 가정을 주장으로 제시한다. B는 포화된 물이 용해력을 잃는다는 세부는 맞지만, 깊은 통로가 오히려 가장 넓다는 핵심과 반대이다. C는 혼합을 지표 지형 형성에 잘못 연결하며 지문에 근거가 없다.
input.explanation_en: The text introduces an old assumption (caves grow largest at surface entry points) and then presents Okafor's finding that two nearly saturated groundwater streams meeting deep underground can regain dissolving power, leading her to conclude that mixing zones may drive much cave enlargement. That is why D is correct. A restates the assumption the text challenges, not its main idea. B correctly notes that saturated water loses dissolving power, but it contradicts the text's point that the deep passages are actually the widest. C links mixing to surface features like sinkholes, which the text never claims.
input.design: To answer, you have to connect two pieces of information: the deep passages are unexpectedly wide, and mixing restores the water's ability to dissolve rock. The wrong choices each reuse a true detail from the text (CO2 at the surface, saturation, surface features) but push it toward the wrong conclusion.

input.passage: In acoustic levitation, an ultrasonic emitter faces a reflector, and the sound waves bouncing between them form a standing wave. Small objects can be trapped at the pressure nodes, points where the sound pressure stays nearly constant and the surrounding pressure pushes inward from both sides. Engineers at several labs have used this technique to hold droplets of pharmaceutical solutions in midair, because a droplet that never touches a container cannot pick up contaminants from its walls. However, the trap works only for objects smaller than roughly half the sound's wavelength, and raising the frequency shortens the wavelength. A team hoping to levitate a larger sample with the same apparatus should therefore ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: lower the emitter's frequency, accepting that the nodes will then be spaced farther apart.
raise the emitter's frequency, since doing so produces more nodes in which samples can be trapped.
replace the reflector with a container, since contact with walls matters less for larger samples.
keep the emitter's frequency unchanged, since node positions depend on the reflector rather than on frequency.
input.explanation: 지문은 물체가 파장의 약 절반보다 작아야 하고, 주파수를 높이면 파장이 짧아진다고 말한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 더 큰 시료를 띄우려면 파장을 늘려야 하므로 주파수를 낮춰야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이며, 파장이 길어지면 노드 간격도 넓어진다는 점과도 맞는다. B는 주파수를 높이면 노드가 많아진다는 점은 그럴듯하지만, 파장이 짧아져 허용 크기가 오히려 줄어든다. C는 지문이 말한 비접촉의 이점(오염 방지)과 어긋나고, D는 크기 한계가 주파수에 달려 있다는 지문 내용과 모순된다.
input.explanation_en: The passage tells you two things: a trapped object has to be smaller than about half the wavelength, and raising the frequency makes the wavelength shorter. Put those together, and you can see that a larger sample needs a longer wavelength, which means a lower frequency. That's why A is correct, and it also fits the fact that longer waves space the nodes farther apart. B sounds reasonable because higher frequency does create more nodes, but it also shortens the wavelength, so the size limit actually gets smaller. C goes against the passage's main point that avoiding contact with walls prevents contamination, and D contradicts the passage, which shows that the size limit depends on frequency.
input.design: To answer, students have to link two facts: the size limit tied to wavelength, and the inverse relationship between frequency and wavelength. B is a trap for readers who skim, because it states something true about nodes but leads to the wrong conclusion.

input.passage: Each autumn, crowds gather along China's Qiantang River to watch its tidal bore, a wall of water that can exceed three meters as the incoming tide rushes upstream against the river's flow. For decades, researchers attributed the bore's height almost entirely to the funnel shape of Hangzhou Bay, which narrows sharply and squeezes the advancing tide. Recent field measurements, however, suggest that the funnel tells only part of the story. Sensors placed below the surface recorded internal waves—oscillations along the boundary between denser salt water and lighter river water—moving ahead of and beneath the bore. When these internal waves lined up with the arriving tide, the bore grew noticeably steeper; when they were out of step, it weakened even though the bay's geometry stayed the same.
input.question: Based on the text, what did the recent field measurements reveal about the Qiantang River's tidal bore?
options: Its strength depends partly on how motion beneath the surface coincides with the tide, not solely on the bay's shape.
Its strength depends mainly on the narrowing of Hangzhou Bay, which compresses the tide as it advances.
Its strength depends partly on the density of the river water, which slows the tide as it moves upstream.
Its strength depends mainly on seasonal crowds of observers, who first noticed changes in the bore's height.
input.explanation: 지문은 새 측정 결과, 만의 지형이 같아도 내부파가 조석과 맞물리느냐에 따라 해일 높이가 달라졌다고 하므로 지형만으로는 설명되지 않는다는 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나온 기존 견해일 뿐, 새 측정은 그것이 '일부'에 불과하다고 했다. C는 밀도가 다른 물을 언급하지만, 지문에서 강물이 조석을 늦춘다고 말하지 않으며 중요한 것은 내부파의 타이밍이다. D는 관람객을 언급하지만, 관람객이 해일 높이를 결정한다거나 변화를 처음 알아챘다는 내용은 없다.
input.explanation_en: The new measurements showed that the bore got steeper or weaker depending on whether internal waves lined up with the tide, even though the bay's shape stayed the same. That makes A correct: the bay's shape isn't the whole explanation. B only restates the older view, and the text says the funnel shape "tells only part of the story." C mentions water density, but the text never says river water slows the tide. What matters is the timing of the internal waves. D brings up the crowds, but the text gives them no role in setting or discovering the bore's height.
input.design: To answer, students have to link the older funnel explanation with the new internal-wave result. B is a tempting wrong answer because it repeats an idea that really is in the passage, and C reuses passage details (salt water and river water) but adds a false cause. All four choices use the same sentence frame.

input.passage: In tribochemical polishing, a rotating pad presses a slurry of oxidizing chemicals and fine silica particles against a semiconductor wafer until its surface is flat to within a few nanometers. Engineers once assumed the particles worked like sandpaper, grinding material away by brute force. Close study of the process has overturned that view.
