"Look at the date," her aunt said. "He wrote this before he called you. This is the man he was in January, not the man he is now. A letter can only tell you how someone felt on the day the ink dried. The phone calls since then are the newer truth."
input.question: Based on the texts, how would the aunt in Text 2 most likely respond to Anjali's reaction to the letter in Text 1?
options: She would say that Anjali is wrong to let the letter outweigh the more recent phone calls.
She would say that Anjali is right to treat the letter as proof that Ravi still wants distance.
She would say that Anjali is wrong to read the letter at all before Ravi explains it.
She would say that Anjali is right to blame the postal service for the letter's cold tone.
input.explanation: Text 1에서 안잘리는 편지를 읽고 최근 몇 달의 통화가 아무 의미 없었던 것처럼 느낀다. Text 2의 이모는 편지가 쓰인 날의 감정만 보여 줄 뿐이고 그 뒤의 통화가 "더 새로운 진실"이라고 말한다. 따라서 이모는 편지를 최근 통화보다 무겁게 여기는 안잘리의 반응이 틀렸다고 할 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 이모가 편지를 지금 라비의 마음으로 보지 않으므로 틀리다. C는 이모가 편지를 읽지 말라고 한 적이 없고 오히려 읽고 날짜를 확인하라고 하므로 틀리다. D는 이모가 문제 삼는 것이 우편이 늦은 사실이 아니라 편지가 쓰인 시점이므로 틀리다.
input.explanation_en: In Text 1, Anjali reads the letter and feels as if months of phone calls "had meant nothing." In Text 2, the aunt says a letter only shows how someone felt on the day it was written, and that the later phone calls are "the newer truth." So the aunt would tell Anjali she is wrong to let the old letter count for more than the recent calls, which makes A correct. B is wrong because the aunt says the letter does not show who Ravi is now. C is wrong because the aunt never tells Anjali not to read it; in fact, she reads it and points out the date. D is wrong because the aunt cares about when the letter was written, not about the mail being slow.
input.design: 이모가 직접 말하는 단서 하나("newer truth")만 보면 풀 수 있고, 추론은 한 단계뿐이다. 선택지 네 개는 모두 "She would say that Anjali is right/wrong to…"라는 같은 틀로 썼다.

input.passage: Potassium-40, a radioactive isotope present in volcanic minerals such as feldspar and biotite, decays into argon-40 at a steady, well-measured rate______ argon is a gas that escapes from molten rock, the mineral's "clock" is effectively reset to zero each time lava erupts and cools. Archaeologists at sites in East Africa's Rift Valley have used this principle to date the ash layers above and below early hominin fossils.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: rate; because
rate, because
rate because
rate; because,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Potassium-40 ... decays ... rate"는 삽입된 동격구를 지나면 하나의 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 "because ... rock, the mineral's clock is ... reset"도 종속절과 주절이 합쳐진 독립절이므로, 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하고 정답은 A이다. B는 쉼표만 써서 because절이 앞 문장을 수식하는 것처럼 보이지만, 뒤에 주절 "the mineral's clock..."이 따로 나오기 때문에 쉼표 접속(comma splice)이 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 세미콜론은 맞지만 접속사 because와 그 주어 argon 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 잘못이다.
input.explanation_en: Once you skip past the appositive, the part before the blank ("Potassium-40 ... decays ... at a steady, well-measured rate") is a complete independent clause. The part after the blank is also an independent clause: the "because" clause leads into its own main clause, "the mineral's 'clock' is effectively reset." Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so A is correct. B can look right if you read the because clause as modifying the first sentence, but the second main clause makes it a comma splice. C fuses the two clauses together with no punctuation at all. D has the right semicolon, but it puts an unneeded comma between "because" and its subject, "argon."
input.design: 긴 동격구 뒤에 나오는 절 경계 문제로, 뒤 절이 because로 시작하기 때문에 쉼표만 써도 될 것처럼 보이게 했다. 주절이 따로 이어진다는 점까지 확인해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.

content.text:
Design: dangling modifier? Or subject-verb agreement after long modifier. Let's do subject-verb with intervening phrase: "The rake, along with the apologies Michael had rehearsed through six winters, ______ in the corner of the garage." Options: "remain" / "were remaining" / "remains"? Need tense context: present narrative? Let's do past tense narrative with "still leaning" ... Better: tense + agreement two-step.

Passage: "Michael had borrowed the rake from Mr. Kowalski one October afternoon, carrying it down the stoop's worn boards with a promise to bring it back by Saturday. Six winters later, the rake, along with the apologies he had rehearsed each time he passed the old man's door, ______ untouched in the corner of the shed, its tines rusted the color of dried leaves."
Options: A "remain" (plural, present), B "were remaining" (plural), C "still sat" — hmm should be same frame. Use: A "have stayed", B "were staying", C "stayed", D "stay". Agreement: singular subject rake; past tense narrative. "stayed" works for both; "have stayed" plural & present perfect; "were" plural; "stay" plural present. All wrong ones plural — but need partial correctness: A could be "has stayed" (singular, but tense shift... "Six winters later" past narrative, has stayed arguably acceptable?). Risky. Keep: A "were left", B "have stayed", C "stayed", D "stay". Fine.

input.passage: Michael had borrowed the rake from Mr. Kowalski one October afternoon, carrying it down the stoop's worn boards with a promise to bring it back by Saturday. Six winters later, the rake, along with the apologies he had rehearsed each time he passed the old man's door, ______ untouched in the corner of the shed, its tines rusted the color of dried leaves.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were left
have stayed
stayed
stay
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the rake'이고, 'along with the apologies...'는 삽입된 수식어구라서 동사의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. 또 지문 전체가 과거 시제(had borrowed, passed)로 서술되므로 동사도 과거형이어야 한다. 단수 주어와 과거 시제를 모두 만족하는 것은 C 'stayed'이다. A는 과거 시제지만 복수형 'were'이므로 틀리고, B는 복수형이면서 현재완료라 과거 서술과 맞지 않는다. D는 복수 현재형이라 수와 시제가 모두 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "the rake." The phrase "along with the apologies..." is just an interrupting modifier, so it doesn't change the number of the verb. The passage is also told in the past tense (had borrowed, passed), so the verb needs to be in the past tense too. Choice C, "stayed," is the only option that fits both a singular subject and the past-tense narration. A is past tense, but "were" is plural; B is a plural present perfect that clashes with the past-tense narration; and D is a plural present-tense form, so it's wrong on both number and tense.
input.design: A plural noun inside an intervening "along with" phrase tempts students to choose a plural verb. To get the answer, students have to check two things: that the verb agrees with the singular subject and that it matches the past-tense narration. Choices A and B each get only part of this right.

content.text:
Need fiction passage, transition at medium. Relationship: concession then reversal without lexical cue, or cause-effect. Let's design: Ailsa had promised her mother she'd bring all mail straight home unopened. The envelope bore her father's handwriting-like... Let's craft:

"The delivery boat bumped against the school pier, and Mr. Fraser handed Ailsa a single envelope addressed to her father, who had died that winter. Ailsa knew her mother would want to open anything of his herself; she had said as much when the first condolence cards arrived. ______ Ailsa slid her thumb under the flap before she reached the end of the pier, unable to wait through the long walk home across the moor."

Answer: Even so, (concession reversal). Distractors: Accordingly, (cause—would mean she obeys; but action contradicts), Similarly, , In other words, . Need B = "Even so,". Options: "Accordingly,", "Even so,", "In particular,", "For this reason,". Two causal — maybe replace one with "Likewise,". Fine.

input.passage: The delivery boat bumped against the island school's pier, and Mr. Fraser handed Ailsa a single envelope addressed to her father, who had drowned the winter before. Ailsa knew her mother would want to open anything of his herself; she had said so quietly, almost fiercely, when the first condolence cards arrived. ______ Ailsa slid her thumb under the flap before she reached the end of the pier, unable to bear the long walk home across the moor without knowing what was inside.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Even so,
In particular,
For this reason,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 어머니가 아버지의 우편물을 직접 열고 싶어 한다는 사실을 아일사가 알고 있었다는 내용이고, 뒷문장은 그럼에도 그녀가 봉투를 열어 버린다는 내용이다. 알고 있던 사실에 반하는 행동이므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 인과 관계를 나타내는데, 어머니의 바람이 오히려 봉투를 여는 이유가 된다는 뜻이 되어 논리가 거꾸로 된다. C는 앞 내용의 구체적인 예를 드는 표현이지만, 봉투를 여는 행동은 어머니의 바람을 구체화하는 예가 아니라 그 바람을 거스르는 행동이다.
input.explanation_en: The first sentence tells you that Ailsa knew her mother wanted to open anything of her father's herself. The next sentence shows Ailsa opening the envelope anyway. Since she acts against what she knows, you need a transition that signals contrast after a concession, so B is correct. A and D signal cause and effect, which would mean her mother's wish was the reason Ailsa opened the letter, and that gets the logic backward. C introduces a specific example of what came before, but opening the envelope goes against the mother's wish rather than illustrating it.
input.design: There's no vocabulary clue; you have to see that knowing the mother's wish and then opening the letter is a concession followed by a reversal. A quick skim might make the two causal options (A and D) look reasonable, and C looks like it could add detail.

input.passage:
Magnetorheological (MR) fluids are suspensions of tiny iron particles in oil. Under ordinary conditions, the particles drift freely and the fluid pours much like motor oil. When a magnetic field is applied, however, the particles line up into chains along the field lines, and within milliseconds the fluid stiffens into a semisolid that strongly resists flow. Removing the field lets the chains collapse, and the fluid returns to its liquid state just as quickly.

Engineers have used this reversible behavior to build shock absorbers whose resistance can be tuned continuously. In a conventional damper, the thickness of the fluid is fixed at manufacture, so the device is a compromise between comfort on smooth roads and control on rough ones. An MR damper, by contrast, pairs the fluid with sensors and an electromagnet, adjusting the field hundreds of times per second so that the damping matches conditions as they change. The same principle now appears in seismic dampers installed in some buildings and bridges.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because iron particles in MR fluids form chains under a magnetic field, MR fluids are thicker than the oils used in conventional shock absorbers.
Because conventional dampers balance comfort against control, engineers have replaced them with MR dampers in most vehicles, buildings, and bridges.
Because MR fluids change state within milliseconds, they are mainly valued for allowing seismic dampers to be installed quickly in existing structures.
Because MR fluids can be switched rapidly and reversibly between liquid and semisolid states, they allow dampers whose resistance adjusts to changing conditions.
input.explanation: 지문은 첫 단락에서 MR 유체가 자기장에 따라 빠르고 가역적으로 액체와 반고체 사이를 오간다는 성질을, 둘째 단락에서 이 성질 덕분에 조건에 맞춰 저항을 조절하는 댐퍼가 가능하다는 점을 설명하므로 D가 중심 내용이다. A는 사슬 형성이라는 세부는 맞지만, 자기장이 없을 때는 모터오일처럼 흐른다고 했으므로 항상 더 두껍다는 진술은 틀리다. B는 기존 댐퍼의 절충이라는 세부는 맞지만, '대부분'을 대체했다는 내용은 지문에 없다. C는 밀리초 단위 변화를 언급하지만, 그 가치를 빠른 설치와 잘못 연결하고 지진 댐퍼라는 부차적 예시를 중심으로 삼는다.
input.explanation_en: The first paragraph explains that MR fluids switch quickly and reversibly between a liquid and a semisolid when a magnetic field is turned on or off. The second paragraph shows how this lets engineers build dampers that adjust to changing conditions, so D states the main idea. A gets the chain formation right, but the text says the fluid pours like motor oil when there's no field, so it isn't always thicker. B correctly mentions the compromise in conventional dampers, but the text never says MR dampers have replaced them in most vehicles or structures. C mentions the millisecond response but wrongly ties its value to quick installation, and it centers on seismic dampers, which are only a passing example.
input.design: Wrong options A, B, and C each borrow a real detail from the text but either distort it or claim more than the text supports. The correct answer requires connecting the fluid's property from paragraph 1 with its application in paragraph 2, and the question doesn't repeat any of the answer's key words.

content.text:
Need fiction passage with transition, answer C. Relationship from logic, e.g., concession then reversal without lexical cue... Let's design: Rune tells himself the boy only watches thermometer because bored. ______, he knows... Better: "In earlier winters, Rune would have dismissed the boy's silence as boredom. ______, he recognized it as worry" — "Now," too cue-ish. Let's do a result: Rune notices boy checking thermometer, then boy asks how thick ice was when Rune was young. Hmm.

Try specification: "The boy had said nothing about the lake all evening. ______, his questions kept circling it: whether the ice-fishing hut..." Answer "Still," (concession then reversal). Distractors: "Indeed," (would need affirm), "As a result," "For example," (questions as example of saying nothing? no). Does "Still," need lexical cue? It's fine. But C must be "Still,".

input.passage: Rune leaned back against the cedar boards and watched his grandson, Eirik, study the thermometer by the door as if it might tell him something besides the heat. The boy had not mentioned the lake once all evening, not even when Rune joked about the old fishing hut. ______ every question Eirik asked seemed to drift toward it: how long the snow used to stay, whether the cousins still skated at Easter, why the hut now sat on the shore instead of out on the ice.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Indeed,
As a result,
Still,
For instance,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 에이리크가 저녁 내내 호수를 한 번도 언급하지 않았다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 그런데도 그의 질문이 모두 호수 쪽으로 향했다고 말하므로 양보 후 반전 관계이며 C가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용을 강조·강화할 때 쓰는데, 뒤 문장은 '언급하지 않았다'를 강화하지 않고 오히려 그와 대조된다. B는 인과를 나타내지만 호수를 언급하지 않은 것이 질문이 호수로 향한 원인이 되지는 않는다. D는 앞 문장의 예시를 제시하는 말인데, 호수로 향하는 질문들은 침묵의 예가 아니라 침묵과 대조되는 내용이다.
input.explanation_en: The first sentence says Eirik never mentioned the lake all evening, and the next sentence says that, even so, every question he asked drifted back toward it. That's a concession followed by a contrast, so C is the answer. A would add emphasis to the previous point, but the second sentence goes against "never mentioned" instead of strengthening it. B signals cause and effect, and staying quiet about the lake doesn't cause his questions to turn toward it. D would bring in an example of the previous claim, but questions that keep circling the lake aren't examples of his silence. They contrast with it.
input.design: There's no contrast word in the passage, so students have to notice that the two sentences pull against each other: he said nothing about the lake, yet his questions kept implying it. A and D tempt skimmers because the questions seem to "illustrate" or "confirm" that he's preoccupied, and B tempts them with a cause-and-effect reading.

content.text:
Need literary passage with transition. Design: concession then reversal, or cause/effect. Let's do: Aksel had told himself the offer was only flattering, nothing he'd seriously consider. ______, he had already looked up apartments near the harbor in Oslo. Answer: "In truth," — contrast between claim and reality. Distractors: "As a result," (cause-effect wrong), "For instance," , "Similarly,". Need partial plausibility. Better: answer C "In truth,". Options: A "Consequently," B "Likewise," C "In truth," D "For example,". Medium okay.

Passage: Aksel leaned back on the cedar bench as the steam rose, the decision pressing against his chest like the heat itself. For two weeks he had insisted to his sister that the Oslo offer was merely flattering, a letter he would answer politely and then forget. ______, he had already memorized the train schedule from the village to the capital and had spent several evenings studying listings for apartments near the city's harbor.

input.passage: Aksel leaned back on the cedar bench as another ladle of water hissed across the stones, and the decision pressed against his chest like the heat itself. For two weeks he had told his sister that the job offer from Oslo was merely flattering, a letter he would answer politely and then forget. ______ he had already memorized the train schedule from the village to the capital and had spent several evenings studying listings for apartments near the city's harbor.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Likewise,
In truth,
For example,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 Aksel이 누나에게 오슬로 제안을 대수롭지 않게 여긴다고 말했다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 그가 실제로는 열차 시간표를 외우고 아파트를 알아보는 등 진지하게 고민해 왔다는 내용이다. 겉으로 한 말과 실제 행동이 대조되므로 '실은'이라는 뜻의 C가 가장 적절하다. A는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 결과로 제시하지만, 제안을 무시하겠다고 말한 것이 이사 준비의 원인이 될 수는 없다. B는 두 문장을 비슷한 내용으로 묶지만 두 문장은 서로 반대된다. D는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 예시로 만들지만, 아파트를 알아본 일은 제안을 잊겠다는 말의 사례가 아니라 그 말과 모순되는 행동이다.
input.explanation_en: The first sentence says Aksel told his sister the Oslo offer was only flattering and that he would forget it. The next sentence shows he had actually been taking it seriously: he memorized train schedules and looked at apartments. Because his words and his actions contrast, C, which means "actually," is the most logical choice. A presents the second sentence as a result of the first, but brushing the offer aside wouldn't make him prepare to move. B suggests the two sentences say similar things, when they actually contradict each other. D treats the apartment search as an example of forgetting the offer, but it's really evidence against that claim.
input.design: 이 문항은 어휘 단서 없이 '말과 행동의 대조'를 파악해야 풀 수 있게 만들었다. 오답은 시간 순서상 인과로 읽히는 A, 두 문장 모두 오슬로를 다룬다는 점에서 유사로 읽히는 B, 뒤 문장이 구체적이라 예시로 읽히는 D로 구성해, 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이도록 했다.

content.text:
Design: literary passage with long nonessential appositive/modifier, then clause boundary.

Passage: "By noon the bronze mirror borrowed from the neighboring shrine was gone, packed by mistake into a tour group's luggage and now somewhere on the coastal highway. Father Ishida, a priest who had performed the harvest rite for thirty years without once altering its ______ the festival crowd watched, hesitant, as he lifted an ordinary lantern where the mirror should have hung."

Hmm, need clause boundary after modifier. Better: "Father Ishida, who had performed the harvest rite for thirty years without once altering its order, did not cancel the ceremony ______ he placed a paper lantern on the altar where the mirror should have stood and began the chant as if nothing were missing."
Options: A ", he" comma splice; B "; and he"? semicolon+and less standard but... avoid. Use: A ", he placed" no—cannot repeat? blank precedes "he"? Let blank be after "ceremony" and options include "he". Options: A ", he" (splice), B "and, he" (wrong comma), C ", instead, he" (splice with adverb), D "; instead, he". Good.

input.passage: By noon the bronze mirror borrowed from the neighboring shrine was gone, packed by mistake into a tour group's luggage and now somewhere on the coastal highway. Father Ishida, who had performed the harvest rite for thirty years without once altering its order, did not cancel the ceremony ______ placed a paper lantern on the altar where the mirror should have stood and began the chant as if nothing were missing.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , he
and, he
, instead, he
; instead, he
input.explanation: 긴 비필수 관계절 뒤에 있는 'Father Ishida ... did not cancel the ceremony'는 독립절이고, 'he placed ...'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이을 수 있으며, 접속부사 instead 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 instead가 들어가 있어도 접속부사는 접속사가 아니므로 역시 comma splice이다. B는 and로 두 절을 잇긴 했지만 and와 he 사이의 쉼표가 불필요하다.
input.explanation_en: Look past the long nonessential clause and you'll see that "Father Ishida ... did not cancel the ceremony" is an independent clause, and "he placed ..." is another one. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, and the conjunctive adverb "instead" takes a comma after it, so D is correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C is still a comma splice even with "instead," because a conjunctive adverb is not a conjunction. B does join the clauses with "and," but the comma between "and" and "he" doesn't belong there.
input.design: A long nonessential relative clause pushes the main verb far from the subject, so students may miss where the clause boundary is. C looks partly right because it has "instead," and B looks partly right because it has a conjunction, so students have to compare them with the correct choice.

input.passage: In the early nineteenth century, much of the indigo grown in Bengal was sold through a few London merchant houses. These houses often agreed among themselves on what they would pay at the city's quarterly auctions. Some historians have argued that this coordination kept prices artificially low, squeezing the planters who shipped dye from India. Economic historian Priya Natarajan finds that account incomplete. __Comparing auction records with planters' private ledgers, she found that in years when the syndicates' agreed bids fell, planters' costs often fell even faster, because the same merchant houses were extending them cheaper credit against future harvests.__ In Natarajan's view, the syndicates controlled the trade less through the auction price itself than through the loans that tied planters to them season after season.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that the merchant syndicates' coordinated bidding had no measurable effect on the prices paid for Bengal indigo.
It gives evidence supporting the historians' claim that the syndicates kept prices low mainly to squeeze Bengal planters.
It explains how the London merchant houses first came to agree among themselves on bids at the quarterly auctions.
It gives evidence that complicates an earlier interpretation and leads to the alternative explanation stated afterward.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 Natarajan이 기존 해석(담합이 가격을 낮춰 재배자를 압박했다)을 '불완전하다'고 본 근거로, 입찰가 하락과 함께 신용 비용도 내려갔다는 기록 비교 결과를 제시한다. 이것이 마지막 문장의 대안적 설명(통제는 대출을 통해 이루어졌다)으로 이어지므로 D가 정답이다. A는 입찰가가 실제로 떨어졌다는 내용과 모순되며, 과장된 주장이다. B는 문장이 가격 하락을 언급하긴 하지만 기존 주장을 지지하는 것이 아니라 복잡하게 만든다는 점을 놓쳤다. C는 담합의 기원을 다루는데, 지문은 그 내용을 전혀 설명하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence gives the evidence behind Natarajan's view that the earlier account is "incomplete." Her records show that planters' costs fell along with the bids, because of cheap credit. That finding leads into the final sentence's alternative explanation, that control worked through loans, so D is correct. A goes too far and contradicts the text: the bids did fall, so the bidding wasn't shown to have no effect. B notices that prices fell, but it misses that the sentence complicates the historians' claim instead of supporting it. C is about how the agreements began, and the text never explains that.
input.design: To answer, students must connect the sentence to "incomplete" before it and to the alternative view after it. B tempts readers who skim and see falling prices, and A tempts readers who overstate the evidence.

input.passage: Tardigrades, microscopic animals found in mosses and soils worldwide, can survive near-total dehydration by entering a state called anhydrobiosis, in which metabolism becomes nearly undetectable. For years, researchers assumed the animals relied mainly on the sugar trehalose, which protects dried cells in organisms such as brine shrimp. Yet many tardigrade species produce little or no trehalose. In 2017, biologist Thomas Boothby and colleagues reported that tardigrades instead make a family of intrinsically disordered proteins, which lack a fixed shape while the animal is hydrated. As water is lost, these proteins form a glassy solid that appears to trap other cellular molecules in place, keeping them from unfolding or clumping together. When the team inserted genes for the proteins into yeast and bacteria, the microbes became noticeably better at surviving drying, suggesting that the proteins themselves, rather than some other feature of tardigrade biology, provide much of the protection.
input.question: According to the text, what did Boothby and colleagues' research indicate about how tardigrades withstand dehydration?
options: Tardigrades withstand dehydration chiefly because they make more trehalose than brine shrimp do, which keeps their cells glassy.
Tardigrades withstand dehydration chiefly because their proteins keep a fixed shape even after water is lost from their cells.
Tardigrades withstand dehydration chiefly because yeast and bacteria living inside them supply genes that resist drying.
Tardigrades withstand dehydration chiefly because certain shapeless proteins solidify as water leaves, holding other molecules steady.
input.explanation: 지문은 많은 완보동물이 트레할로스를 거의 만들지 않으며, 대신 수화 상태에서 고정된 형태가 없는 단백질이 탈수 시 유리질 고체가 되어 다른 분자의 변성·응집을 막는다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 '유리질'이라는 단어를 맞게 썼지만 트레할로스 의존은 지문이 반박한 기존 가정이다. B는 단백질이 보호한다는 점은 맞으나, 실제로는 수화 상태에서 형태가 없다가 건조 시 고체화하는 것이므로 '고정된 형태 유지'는 틀렸다. C는 효모·세균이 등장하지만 이는 유전자를 주입받은 실험 대상이지 유전자 공급원이 아니다.
input.explanation_en: D is correct: the text says many tardigrades make little trehalose and instead produce proteins with no fixed shape while hydrated, which form a glassy solid during drying that keeps other molecules from unfolding or clumping. A borrows the word "glassy," but relying on trehalose is the earlier assumption the text challenges. B is right that proteins protect the cells, but it gets their behavior backward, since the proteins lack a fixed shape and then solidify. C mentions yeast and bacteria, but those microbes received the tardigrade genes in the experiment. They weren't the source of the genes.
input.design: 각 오답이 지문의 실제 요소(유리질, 단백질, 효모·세균)를 일부 활용하지만 관계를 뒤틀어, 기존 가정과 새 발견을 구분하고 실험의 방향을 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하게 했다.

input.passage: For three years, Morag had watched Miss Fraser chalk the date onto the blackboard each morning, and she knew the looping shape of every numeral by heart. Today the chalk skittered, leaving a seven that wavered like marram grass in the wind off the Sound. No one in the cramped schoolroom, not even the minister's son, who noticed everything and repeated most of ______ said a word about it. Morag, however, slid her own hands beneath the desk and began, very quietly, to count the tremors.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: it,
it
it;
it—
input.design: Two nested nonessential elements ("not even the minister's son" and the "who" clause) separate the subject "No one" from the verb "said." Students must see that both open with commas and so must close with a comma before the main verb. The semicolon and dash distractors look like clause boundaries a skimming reader might expect there.
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "No one"이고 본동사는 "said"이다. 그 사이에 쉼표로 시작하는 비필수 삽입 요소 "not even the minister's son"과 "who noticed everything and repeated most of it"이 들어가 있으므로, 여는 쉼표에 맞춰 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 닫는 쉼표가 없어서 "it said"가 하나로 붙어 읽히고, 그 결과 주어와 동사의 연결이 흐려진다. C의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데, 앞부분에는 본동사가 없어 독립절이 아니다. D의 대시는 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 닫을 수 없으므로 부호의 짝이 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "No one," and its main verb is "said." Between them are two nonessential elements, "not even the minister's son" and "who noticed everything and repeated most of it." Both open with commas, so they have to close with a comma before the verb. That makes A correct. B leaves out the closing comma, so "it said" runs together and the subject–verb link gets blurred. C uses a semicolon, which needs an independent clause on both sides, but the part before the blank has no main verb yet. D uses a dash, which can't close an interruption that opened with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match.

input.passage: In 1968, psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson reported that elementary students whom teachers had been told were about to "bloom" intellectually showed larger IQ gains over a school year than their classmates, even though the "bloomers" had actually been chosen at random. The finding, dubbed the Pygmalion effect, was widely taken to show that teacher expectations can powerfully reshape student achievement. Later researchers, however, were more cautious. When education scholar Lee Jussim and colleagues reviewed decades of follow-up studies, they found that teacher expectations do predict student outcomes, but mostly because teachers' judgments are fairly accurate reflections of students' existing abilities. The portion of student achievement actually caused by teachers' beliefs turned out to be real but small, though somewhat larger for students from groups that teachers tended to stereotype negatively.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Research showing that teachers' beliefs strongly shape student achievement has been confirmed by later studies, especially for students who face negative stereotypes.
Follow-up studies revealed that the Pygmalion effect was produced entirely by flaws in how Rosenthal and Jacobson randomly selected their students.
Teachers' expectations are generally inaccurate, which explains why they have only a small influence on how students actually perform.
Later research suggests that teacher expectations influence student achievement less than an early study implied, since those expectations largely mirror students' actual abilities.
input.explanation: 지문은 1968년 연구가 교사 기대의 강력한 영향을 보여 준 것으로 받아들여졌지만, 이후 연구에서 그 기대가 대체로 학생의 실제 능력을 정확히 반영하며 기대 자체가 일으키는 효과는 작다는 결과가 나왔다고 설명한다. 이 두 정보를 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 고정관념 집단에서 효과가 더 크다는 세부는 맞지만, '강한 영향이 확인되었다'는 것은 지문의 결론과 반대다. B는 효과가 '전적으로' 오류라고 하지만 지문은 효과가 실재하되 작다고 한다. C는 효과가 작다는 점은 맞지만, 교사의 판단이 '부정확하다'고 한 것은 지문에서 '상당히 정확하다'고 한 것과 반대다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the 1968 study was taken as proof that teacher expectations powerfully shape achievement, but later reviews found that those expectations mostly reflect students' real abilities, and the part actually caused by teachers' beliefs is small. D links these two ideas, so it's the correct answer. A gets one detail right (the effect is larger for stereotyped students), but it says the strong effect was confirmed, which is the opposite of the text's conclusion. B says the effect came entirely from flaws, yet the text calls the effect real, just small. C is right that the influence is small, but it calls teachers' judgments inaccurate, while the text describes them as fairly accurate.
input.design: 오답 A와 C가 각각 부분적으로 맞는 세부(고정관념 집단, 작은 효과)를 담아, 초기 결과와 후속 결과를 연결해야만 배제되도록 했다. B는 과장된 버전이다.

input.passage:
Text 1
Metamaterials are engineered structures built from tiny repeating units, such as metal rings and wires, arranged in patterns. Because these units resonate with incoming waves, some metamaterials bend light in the "wrong" direction, giving them a negative refractive index. Many writers predict that such materials will soon make practical invisibility cloaks for everyday objects.

Text 2
Negative refraction in metamaterials is real and well tested, but it usually works only in a narrow band of wavelengths, near the frequency where the structures resonate. Outside that band, the effect fades, and the materials also absorb much of the energy passing through them. For now, a cloak that hides an object from ordinary visible light, which spans many wavelengths, remains far beyond reach.
input.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the prediction described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the prediction is too hopeful because the effect it depends on works only over a limited range of wavelengths
By arguing that the prediction is mistaken because metamaterials have never actually been shown to bend light in a negative direction
By arguing that the prediction is too cautious because metamaterials already hide objects from all kinds of visible light
By arguing that the prediction is irrelevant because metamaterials are made from natural crystals rather than engineered units
input.explanation: Text 2는 음의 굴절이 실제로 있다고 인정하지만, 공명 주파수 근처의 좁은 파장대에서만 작동하므로 가시광선 전체를 가리는 투명 망토는 아직 먼 이야기라고 말한다. 따라서 Text 1의 예측이 지나치게 낙관적이라고 볼 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 이 효과를 '실제로 있고 충분히 검증되었다'고 한 것과 어긋난다. C는 Text 2의 조심스러운 태도와 정반대이다. D는 메타물질이 인공 구조물이라는 두 지문의 설명과 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Text 2 agrees that negative refraction is real, but it says the effect works only in a narrow band of wavelengths near resonance, so a cloak for visible light, which covers many wavelengths, is still far off. That means the author would see Text 1's prediction as too hopeful, so A is correct. B is wrong because Text 2 says the effect is "real and well tested." C is wrong because it's the opposite of Text 2's cautious view. D is wrong because both texts describe metamaterials as engineered structures, not natural crystals.
input.design: Text 2의 한계 지적(좁은 파장대)을 하나만 찾으면 풀리는 easy 문항이다. 오답은 모두 같은 "By arguing that the prediction is ... because ..." 틀로 썼고, 각각 효과 자체를 부정하는 것, 방향을 거꾸로 잡는 것, 사실을 잘못 아는 것이라는 흔한 오개념을 담았다.

input.passage:
Text 1
Many art historians describe the minaret mainly as a symbol. In their view, the tall tower rising above a mosque was built to mark the building as a place of worship and to show the power of the rulers who paid for it. Its height, they argue, was about meaning, not use.

Text 2
Before loudspeakers, the muezzin had to climb the minaret five times a day to call people to prayer. Tests in old mosques show that a voice from the top of a tower travels much farther over rooftops than a voice from the ground. For this reason, the minaret's height was first of all a practical answer to the problem of being heard across a city.
input.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the art historians' view described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the minaret's height mattered mostly because it showed the power of the rulers who paid for it
By arguing that the minaret's height mattered mostly because it made the mosque look different from nearby homes
By arguing that the minaret's height mattered mostly because loudspeakers later made the tower unnecessary
By arguing that the minaret's height mattered mostly because it helped the muezzin's voice reach distant listeners
input.explanation: Text 1은 미나렛의 높이가 쓰임이 아니라 상징을 위한 것이라고 보고, Text 2는 높이가 소리를 도시 전체에 전달하는 실용적 해결책이었다고 주장하므로 정답은 D이다. A는 Text 1의 견해를 그대로 되풀이한 것이라 Text 2의 반응이 될 수 없다. B 역시 건물을 구별하는 상징적 기능으로, Text 2가 강조하는 점이 아니다. C는 Text 2가 확성기를 언급하긴 하지만 높이가 중요했던 이유로 제시한 것이 아니다.
input.explanation_en: Text 1 says the minaret's height was about meaning, not use, while Text 2 says the height was mainly a practical way to make the call to prayer heard across a city, so D is correct. A just repeats Text 1's own view, so it can't be how Text 2's author would push back. B also describes a symbolic purpose (marking the building), which is not what Text 2 stresses. C mentions loudspeakers, but Text 2 brings them up only to describe the time before them, not as the reason height mattered.
input.design: Text 2가 Text 1과 직접 반대되는 주장 하나를 명시적으로 펴므로, 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답들은 같은 문장 틀을 쓰면서 Text 1의 상징론을 되풀이하거나 지문의 세부 내용을 잘못 활용한다.

input.passage: In Plato's early dialogues, Socrates rarely delivers a lesson. Instead, he asks an interlocutor to define a concept such as courage or piety, then poses questions that expose contradictions in each proposed definition. Many modern instructors cite these exchanges as a model for discussion-based teaching, in which students reach understanding by answering rather than listening. __Yet the dialogues themselves seldom end in understanding: the Euthyphro, for example, closes with its title character hurrying away, no closer to defining piety than when he began.__ Some scholars argue that this unresolved ending is the point, since Socrates' aim was to replace false confidence with an awareness of one's own ignorance, an outcome that teachers who prize tidy conclusions may overlook.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives an example showing how Socrates' questions led an interlocutor to a correct definition of a concept.
It offers evidence that modern instructors have misread which dialogues best represent Socrates' method.
It identifies a flaw in Socrates' reasoning that later scholars have tried to correct.
It introduces a feature of the dialogues that complicates the way the method is often applied in classrooms.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 시작해, 현대 교사들이 학생이 이해에 도달하는 모델로 대화편을 인용한다는 앞 문장과 달리 대화편이 대개 결론 없이 끝난다는 점을 제시하며, 마지막 문장은 이 미해결이 의도된 것이고 깔끔한 결론을 중시하는 교사들이 놓칠 수 있다고 설명한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 Euthyphro가 정의에 도달하지 못했다는 내용과 반대된다. B는 교사들을 언급하지만, 교사들이 어떤 대화편을 골랐는지가 아니라 결말의 성격이 쟁점이다. C는 결론이 없다는 점을 소크라테스 추론의 결함으로 보지만, 지문은 그것이 의도된 목적일 수 있다고 본다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet." It contrasts the earlier claim that teachers use the dialogues as a model for reaching understanding with the fact that the dialogues usually end without any resolution. The final sentence then says this lack of resolution may be the point, which teachers who prize tidy conclusions may miss, so D is correct. A is wrong because Euthyphro gets no closer to a definition at all. B mentions teachers, but the issue is how the dialogues end, not which dialogues teachers chose. C treats the missing conclusion as a flaw in Socrates' reasoning, while the text suggests it may have been his aim.
input.design: 이 문항은 앞 문장과의 대조(Yet)와 뒤 문장의 재해석을 연결해야 풀 수 있게 만들었다. B와 C는 교사·학자에 대한 부분적 근거가 있어 지문과 비교해야만 배제된다.

input.passage: After his welding shift ended at the mountain depot, Francisco carried a bag of clay to the small workroom behind the supply shed. The potter's wheel there had belonged to a retired mechanic, and no one else had touched it in years. On his first evening, the clay collapsed under his hands four times ______ he kept wetting his palms and starting again.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: times,
times
times, but
times, and, but
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the clay collapsed ... four times"와 뒤 "he kept wetting his palms ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 연결할 수 있으므로 C(쉼표 + but)가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호도 접속사도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and와 but을 함께 써서 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Look at both sides of the blank: "the clay collapsed under his hands four times" and "he kept wetting his palms and starting again" are each independent clauses. You can join two independent clauses with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so C (a comma followed by "but") is correct. A uses only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. B has no punctuation and no conjunction, so it makes a run-on sentence. D puts two coordinating conjunctions ("and" and "but") together, which isn't grammatical.
input.design: 독립절 두 개가 빈칸 양쪽에 바로 보이는 easy 문항으로, 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 접속사를 겹쳐 쓴 오류를 오답으로 두었다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the late 1800s, Jamaican smallholders grew bananas on small plots and sold them to many competing foreign shippers.
- By the early 1900s, the Boston-based United Fruit Company had absorbed most rival shippers on the island.
- With few other buyers left, growers had little choice but to accept the prices the company offered—a market condition economists call monopsony.
- In some seasons, the company rejected bunches it judged too small, leaving growers with unsold fruit.
- Low earnings pushed thousands of Jamaican workers to migrate to Panama, Costa Rica, and Cuba for wage labor.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize how a change in the number of buyers shifted bargaining power in Jamaica's banana trade. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In some seasons, United Fruit rejected banana bunches it judged too small, so Jamaican growers were left holding fruit they could not sell.
Once United Fruit had absorbed most rival shippers, Jamaican growers who had once sold to many competing buyers were left to accept whatever prices the company set.
From small-plot farming in the 1800s to company consolidation and widespread migration abroad, Jamaica's banana economy underwent many changes over several decades.
Because banana earnings were low, thousands of Jamaican workers left the island to take wage jobs in Panama, Costa Rica, and Cuba.
input.explanation: 정답 B: 많은 경쟁 구매자→United Fruit의 경쟁사 흡수→재배자가 가격을 그대로 받아들여야 함이라는 흐름으로, 구매자 수의 변화가 협상력을 어떻게 옮겼는지 강조한다. A: 너무 세부적이다. 작은 송이를 거부한 사례 하나만 들고, 구매자 수가 줄었다는 점은 빠져 있다. C: 너무 포괄적이다. 수십 년간의 변화를 나열하기만 해서 협상력이라는 초점이 흐려진다. D: 목표와 다른 항목(노동 이주)을 강조한다. 이주는 결과일 뿐, 구매자 수와 협상력의 관계는 다루지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: B is correct. It links the change from many competing buyers to the company absorbing its rivals, and then to growers having to accept whatever prices the company set. That shows how fewer buyers moved bargaining power to United Fruit. A is too narrow: it gives one example (rejected bunches) and never mentions the drop in the number of buyers. C is too broad: it lists decades of changes and loses the focus on bargaining power. D highlights a different note, labor migration, which was an effect and doesn't explain how buyer numbers changed bargaining power.
input.design: 목표는 '구매자 수 변화에 따른 협상력 이동'을 강조하는 것이다. 정답은 노트 1~3을 종합한다. 오답은 각각 지나치게 세부적인 사례(노트 4), 지나치게 포괄적인 개관, 무관한 항목(이주) 강조로 구성했다. 질문에는 정답의 핵심어(absorbed, prices)를 쓰지 않았다.

input.passage: The ferry to Dominica was still an hour from Roseau when the radio crackled with news of a sailor stranded on a reef somewhere off the northern coast, his instruments dead. Thomas, who had fished these waters for thirty years, felt the weight in his jacket before he understood it: the brass compass that he had borrowed from old Delphine's boatyard one stormy spring, along with two coils of rope and a faded tide chart, ______ against his hip as the ferry rounded the point.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was pressing
were pressing
pressing
having pressed
input.explanation: 콜론 뒤 절의 주어는 단수 'the brass compass'이고, 'that he had borrowed...'와 'along with two coils of rope and a faded tide chart'는 수식어일 뿐이므로 절에는 단수 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(rope, chart)에 끌린 복수형이라 주어와 수가 맞지 않는다. 'along with'는 주어를 복수로 만들지 않는다. C와 D는 분사라서 콜론 뒤 절에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 절이 되지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the clause after the colon is the singular noun "the brass compass." The phrases "that he had borrowed..." and "along with two coils of rope and a faded tide chart" only modify it, so the clause needs a singular main verb, and that makes A correct. B does supply a main verb, but it's plural because it matches the nearby nouns "rope" and "chart." Remember that "along with" doesn't make a subject plural. C and D are participles, so the clause after the colon would be left with no main verb and wouldn't be a complete clause.
input.design: 긴 관계절과 'along with' 복수 명사구가 단수 주어와 빈칸 사이에 있어, 정동사 필요성과 수일치를 둘 다 판단해야 한다.

input.passage: When threatened by a crab or fish, many sea cucumbers do something that seems self-defeating: they contract their body walls and expel part of their internal organs, including portions of the gut and respiratory tree, through a rupture in the body. The ejected tissue can entangle or distract a predator while the sea cucumber creeps away. Biologists once assumed that such a drastic loss must leave the animal crippled for most of its remaining life. __Studies of the species Holothuria glaberrima, however, have shown that a functional new gut can form within about three weeks, built largely by cells in the connective tissue lining the body cavity that lose their specialized character and begin dividing.__ This finding has made sea cucumbers a model for researchers asking why some animals can rebuild complex organs while mammals generally cannot.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the expelled organs are effective at entangling predators, supporting the explanation offered earlier in the text.
It describes a cellular process that biologists had predicted would be too slow to repair a sea cucumber's damaged organs.
It presents findings that challenge an earlier assumption about the consequences of the sea cucumber's defensive behavior.
It explains why mammals cannot regenerate organs, setting up the comparison made in the final sentence.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 시작해, 내장 방출 후 동물이 평생 불구가 될 것이라는 앞 문장의 가정을 약 3주 만의 장 재생이라는 연구 결과로 반박하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 방출 조직이 포식자를 방해한다는 앞 내용과 연결되지만, 밑줄 문장은 방어 효과가 아니라 재생을 다룬다. B는 세포 과정을 언급한다는 점은 맞지만, 생물학자들이 그 과정이 느릴 것이라 예측했다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 마지막 문장의 포유류 비교를 끌어오지만, 밑줄 문장은 포유류가 재생하지 못하는 이유를 설명하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence opens with "however" and reports that a new gut forms in about three weeks, which contradicts the earlier assumption that losing organs would leave the animal crippled for good. That makes C correct. A ties back to the earlier point about tangling up predators, but the underlined sentence is about regrowing organs, not about how well the defense works. B is right that the sentence describes a cellular process, but the text never says biologists predicted that process would be too slow. D borrows the mammal comparison from the last sentence, but the underlined sentence doesn't explain why mammals can't regenerate organs.
input.design: Two steps are needed: notice that "however" contrasts with the assumption in the previous sentence, and then check what the underlined sentence actually contains. Each wrong answer borrows a real detail from the passage (the predator defense, the cell process, the mammal comparison) but gives it the wrong function.
